sentences.zh: 張允登，漢州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yundeng was a native of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yundeng came from Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知咸寧、咸陽，有善政。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Xianning and Xianyang, and his governance was benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Xianning and Xianyang, where his administration won praise.

sentences.zh: 其成進士，出湯賓尹之門，賓尹弗善也，而東林以賓尹故，惡之。

translations.literal: When he became a metropolitan graduate he had come from the school of Tang Binyi; Binyi did not favor him, and because of Binyi the Donglin faction hated him.
translations.idiomatic: As a new jinshi he had studied under Tang Binyi, whom he had displeased; the Donglin partisans therefore turned against him on Binyi's account.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，得刑部主事，累遷河西兵備副使。

translations.literal: Rated outstanding, he was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments and was promoted in due course to Assistant Military Commissioner for the Hexi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After an outstanding evaluation he entered the Ministry of Punishments as a principal secretary and rose step by step to Assistant Military Commissioner for the Hexi circuit.

sentences.zh: 鄜、延歲饑，亟遭盜，允登拊循備至，士民德之。

translations.literal: Fuzhou and Yan'an suffered famine year after year and were repeatedly troubled by bandits; Yundeng comforted and cared for the people with the utmost diligence, and officials and commoners were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou and Yan'an endured famine year after year and repeated raids; Yundeng comforted and provisioned the people with tireless care, and gentry and commoners alike were devoted to him.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年閏十一月督餉至甘泉，降卒潛與流賊通，殺知縣郭永固，劫餉。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month of the fourth year of Chongzhen, while supervising grain transport at Ganquan, surrendered troops secretly colluded with roving bandits, killed Magistrate Guo Yonggu, and plundered the provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month of the fourth year of Chongzhen he was escorting grain rations to Ganquan when surrendered soldiers secretly joined the roving bandits, killed Magistrate Guo Yonggu, and seized the supplies.

sentences.zh: 允登力禦，不敵死。

translations.literal: Yundeng resisted with all his strength but was overwhelmed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yundeng fought back with all his strength but was overpowered and killed.

sentences.zh: 鄜人素服迎其喪，哭聲震十里，罷市三日。

translations.literal: The people of Fuzhou met his bier in plain white mourning dress; lamentation shook the countryside for ten li, and markets were closed for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fuzhou went out in plain white to receive his coffin; mourning cries were heard for ten li around, and the markets closed for three days.

sentences.zh: 當是時，流賊日熾，總督洪承疇往來奔擊，日不暇給。

translations.literal: At that time roving bandits grew fiercer by the day; Governor-General Hong Chengchou rushed back and forth in pursuit, with scarcely a moment to spare.
translations.idiomatic: By then the roving bandits were growing stronger daily; Governor-General Hong Chengchou raced from place to place in pursuit and scarcely had a moment's rest.

sentences.zh: 逾月陷宜君，又陷葭州，僉事郭景嵩死之。

translations.literal: A month later they captured Yijun, then Jiazhou; Vice Commissioner Guo Jingsong died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month they took Yijun and then Jiazhou; Vice Commissioner Guo Jingsong died defending the latter.

sentences.zh: 明年二月陷鄜州，兵備副使郭應響死之。

translations.literal: The following second month they took Fuzhou; Assistant Military Commissioner Guo Yingxiang died defending it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, they captured Fuzhou; Assistant Military Commissioner Guo Yingxiang died in its defense.

sentences.zh: 應響，福清人，萬歷丙午舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: Yingxiang, a native of Fuqing, had ranked first in the provincial examination in the bingwu year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiang was a native of Fuqing and had placed first in the provincial examinations in the bingwu year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 寧塞余賊來犯，應響禦之，斬賊常山虎等十五人。

translations.literal: When remnant bandits from Ningsai attacked, Yingxiang repelled them and beheaded fifteen men including the bandit Changshanhu.
translations.idiomatic: When remnant bandits from Ningsai raided the district, Yingxiang drove them off and beheaded fifteen of them, including the outlaw Changshanhu.

sentences.zh: 至是，混天猴率眾夜突至，應響登北關，集士卒拒守，手殺三賊，力不支遂死。

translations.literal: On this occasion Huntianhou led his host in a night assault; Yingxiang went up the North Gate, gathered troops to hold the wall, and with his own hand killed three bandits, but his strength gave out and he fell.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Huntianhou led his men in a night assault; Yingxiang mounted the North Gate, rallied the garrison to hold the wall, and killed three bandits with his own hand before his strength failed and he fell.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈光祿寺少卿，謚忠烈，予祭葬，蔭一子入監讀書。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, granted the posthumous name Zhonglie, given state sacrifice and burial, and one son was granted entrance to the Directorate of Education as a student by yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court he was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, given the posthumous name Loyal and Fierce, granted state sacrifices and burial, and one son was admitted to the Directorate of Education by yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 張光奎，澤州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangkui was a native of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangkui came from Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 仕至山東右參政。

translations.literal: In office he rose to Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen to Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，流賊躪山西，監司王肇生以便宜署歙人吳開先為將，使擊賊，戰澤州城西。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen roving bandits overran Shanxi; Supervising Secretary Wang Zhaosheng, acting on discretionary authority, appointed Wu Kaixian of She county as general and sent him to strike the bandits; they fought west of Zezhou city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen roving bandits swept through Shanxi; Supervising Secretary Wang Zhaosheng, exercising emergency powers, appointed Wu Kaixian of She county as a general and sent him against the bandits; the battle was fought west of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 賊敗去，從沁水轉掠陽城。

translations.literal: The bandits were defeated and withdrew, then from Qinshui turned to plunder Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were beaten off but then swung from Qinshui to raid Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 開先恃勇渡沁，戰北留墩下，擊斬數百人，炮盡無援，一軍盡沒。

translations.literal: Kaixian, trusting in his courage, crossed the Qin River and fought below Beiliudun, killing several hundred in the assault; when his cannon were spent and no reinforcements came, his whole force was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixian, relying on his boldness, crossed the Qin and fought below Beiliudun, cutting down several hundred men; when his artillery was exhausted and no aid arrived, his entire command perished.

sentences.zh: 賊乃再犯澤州，光奎方里居，與兄守備光璽、千總劉自安等率眾固守八日，援兵不至，城陷，並死之。

translations.literal: The bandits then attacked Zezhou again; Guangkui was living at home and, with his elder brother the garrison commander Guangxi, Company Commander Liu Zi'an, and others, led the people in a stubborn defense for eight days; when relief did not arrive the city fell and all died together.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then struck Zezhou again; Guangkui was at home on leave and, with his elder brother the garrison commander Guangxi, Company Commander Liu Zi'an, and others, led the townspeople in an eight-day defense; when no relief came the city fell and they all died together.

sentences.zh: 澤，大州也，遠近為震動。

translations.literal: Zezhou was a great prefecture, and the shock was felt far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Zezhou was a major prefecture, and the news sent shock through the region.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈光祿卿，光璽等贈恤有差。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Guangkui was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Guangxi and the others received graded posthumous honors and relief.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court Guangkui was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Guangxi and the others received posthumous honors and relief in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 是歲，紫金梁等寇遼州，裏居行人楊於楷與主事張友程，佐知州信陽李呈章拒守，力屈城陷，於楷被執，罵賊死。

translations.literal: That year Zijinliang and others raided Liaozhou; the retired Ministry of Rites messenger Yang Yukai and Principal Secretary Zhang Youcheng assisted Magistrate Li Chengzhang of Xinyang in the defense; when their strength failed the city fell; Yukai was seized and died cursing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zijinliang and others attacked Liaozhou; the retired Ministry of Rites messenger Yang Yukai and Principal Secretary Zhang Youcheng aided Magistrate Li Chengzhang of Xinyang in holding the city; when resistance collapsed Yukai was captured and died reviling the bandits.

sentences.zh: 呈章、友程及舉人趙一亨、侯標並死之。

translations.literal: Chengzhang, Youcheng, and the licentiates Zhao Yiheng and Hou Biao all died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhang, Youcheng, and the licentiates Zhao Yiheng and Hou Biao likewise perished.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，賊陷和順，裏居昌平副使樂濟眾被傷，不屈，投井死。

translations.literal: The next year, in the sixth month, bandits took Heshun; the retired Changping Vice Commissioner Yue Jizhong was wounded, refused to submit, and threw himself into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: The following sixth month the bandits took Heshun; the retired Changping Vice Commissioner Yue Jizhong was wounded, would not yield, and drowned himself in a well.

sentences.zh: 贈於楷光祿少卿，濟眾太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Yukai was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Jizhong was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Yukai was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Jizhong was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 有徐明揚者，浮梁人，由選貢生為平順知縣。

translations.literal: There was one Xu Mingyang, a native of Fuliang, who through selection as a tribute student became magistrate of Pingshun.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Xu Mingyang of Fuliang, who entered office as magistrate of Pingshun through the tribute-student route.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，賊來犯，設策守禦，城破不屈死。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year bandits came to attack; he devised measures to defend the city, and when it fell he refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year the bandits attacked; he devised a defense, and when the city fell he would not submit and was killed.

sentences.zh: 李中正，盧氏人。

translations.literal: Li Zhongzheng was a native of Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongzheng came from Lushi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末，舉會試，以天啟二年赴廷對，授承天府推官，遷兵部主事。

translations.literal: At the end of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination; in the second year of Tianqi he attended the palace examination and was appointed investigating censor of Chengtian Prefecture, then transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination; in the second year of Tianqi he took the palace examination and was appointed investigating censor of Chengtian Prefecture, later transferring to the Ministry of War as a principal secretary.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，謝病歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 六年，群盜大亂河北。

translations.literal: In the sixth year bandit hosts threw Hebei into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year bandit armies threw Hebei into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 其冬，乘冰渡河，遂由澠池犯盧氏。

translations.literal: That winter they crossed the river on the ice and then, by way of Mianchi, invaded Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they crossed the frozen river and advanced through Mianchi against Lushi.

sentences.zh: 中州承平久，不設備。

translations.literal: The central provinces had long been at peace and were unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: The central provinces had known peace for so long that they were wholly unprepared.

sentences.zh: 驟聞賊至，吏民惶駴，知縣金會嘉棄城遁。

translations.literal: Suddenly hearing that bandits had arrived, officials and people were terrified; Magistrate Jin Huijia abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the sudden news of the bandits, officials and townspeople panicked; Magistrate Jin Huijia abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊入城，中正勒家眾及里中壯士奮擊，眾寡不敵，力戰死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the bandits entered the city; Zhongzheng mustered his household and stalwarts of the neighborhood to strike back; outnumbered, he fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the bandits entered the city; Zhongzheng rallied his household and local stalwarts to fight back; outnumbered, he battled until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 賊縱掠城中，執舉人靳謙書，使跪，不屈，大罵而死。

translations.literal: The bandits plundered the city at will; they seized the licentiate Jin Qianshu, made him kneel, and when he would not submit he cursed them loudly and died.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits looted the city at will; they seized the licentiate Jin Qianshu and forced him to kneel; he refused and died after hurling abuse at them.

sentences.zh: 賊以是冬始入河南，自是屢陷名城，殺將吏無算，鄉官舉貢多被難。

translations.literal: The bandits first entered Henan that winter; thereafter they repeatedly took famous cities and killed countless commanders and officials, and many local gentry and licentiates met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits first entered Henan that winter; from then on they repeatedly captured great cities and killed commanders and officials beyond count, while many local gentry and licentiates perished in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 其宜陽馬足輕，靈寶許煇，新安劉君培、馬山、李登英，偃師裴君合，陜州張我正、張我德，孟津孫挺生，嵩縣傅世濟、李佩玉，上蔡劉時寵輩，則先後以布衣抗節顯。

translations.literal: Among them Ma Zuqing of Yiyang, Xu Hui of Lingbao, Liu Junpei, Ma Shan, and Li Dengying of Xin'an, Pei Junhe of Yanshi, Zhang Wozheng and Zhang Wode of Shaanzhou, Sun Tingsheng of Mengjin, Fu Shiji and Li Peiyu of Song county, Liu Shichong of Shangcai and others in succession won fame as commoners who upheld their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were Ma Zuqing of Yiyang, Xu Hui of Lingbao, Liu Junpei, Ma Shan, and Li Dengying of Xin'an, Pei Junhe of Yanshi, Zhang Wozheng and Zhang Wode of Shaanzhou, Sun Tingsheng of Mengjin, Fu Shiji and Li Peiyu of Song county, and Liu Shichong of Shangcai—each in turn distinguished himself as a commoner who held fast to his principles.

sentences.zh: 足輕，性孝友。

translations.literal: Zuqing was by nature filial and brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: Zuqing was known for filial devotion and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 弟惑婦言，迫分產，乃取田磽薄者自予。

translations.literal: His younger brother was swayed by his wife's words and pressed for a division of the estate; he therefore took the poorer, thinner plots for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother, swayed by his wife, pressed for a division of the family property, Zuqing kept only the poorer, thinner fields for himself.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末，歲大兇，出粟六百石以振，焚券千余。

translations.literal: At the end of Wanli, when the year was fiercely famine-stricken, he dispensed six hundred dan of grain for relief and burned more than a thousand debt notes.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Wanli, in a year of terrible famine, he gave out six hundred dan of grain for relief and burned more than a thousand IOUs.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年冬，流賊渡河而南，挈家避之石龍崖。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Chongzhen roving bandits crossed the river southward; he took his family to take refuge at Shilong Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year of Chongzhen the roving bandits crossed the river heading south, and he took his family to shelter at Shilong Cliff.

sentences.zh: 三女皆殊色，慮賊汙，悉投崖死。

translations.literal: His three daughters were all strikingly beautiful; fearing violation by bandits, they all leaped from the cliff to their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: His three daughters were all exceptionally beautiful; fearing defilement by the bandits, they threw themselves from the cliff and died.

sentences.zh: 足輕被執，厲聲大罵。

translations.literal: Zuqing was seized and cursed them loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Zuqing was captured and hurled abuse at them in a thunderous voice.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，並三子殺之。

translations.literal: In anger the bandits killed him together with his three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits killed him along with his three sons.

sentences.zh: 家眾皆遇害，惟存次子駿一人，後登鄉薦。

translations.literal: The entire household perished except his second son Jun alone, who later passed the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: The whole household was killed; only his second son, Jun, survived and later passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 煇為縣陰陽官，為賊所掠，大罵見殺。

translations.literal: Hui served as the county yin-yang official; when seized by bandits he cursed them loudly and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui served as the county yin-yang official; when the bandits seized him he cursed them loudly and was killed.

sentences.zh: 君培有義行，攜子及從孫避難，道遇賊，欲殺其從孫。

translations.literal: Junpei was known for righteous conduct; fleeing with his son and younger nephew, they met bandits on the road who wished to kill the nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Junpei was known for righteous conduct; while fleeing with his son and a younger nephew he met bandits on the road who meant to kill the boy.

sentences.zh: 君培曰：「我尚有男，此子乃遺孤，幸舍之而殺我。

translations.literal: Junpei said, I still have a grown son; this boy is an orphan—please spare him and kill me instead.
translations.idiomatic: Junpei said, "I still have a grown son; this child is an orphan. Please spare him and kill me instead."

sentences.zh: 」賊如其言，二子獲免。

translations.literal: The bandits did as he asked, and the two boys were spared.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits did as he asked, and both boys were spared.

sentences.zh: 山性剛直，土寇於大中陷新安，獲山，使負米。

translations.literal: Shan was stiff and upright in character; when local bandits under Yu Dazhong took Xin'an, they seized Shan and made him carry grain.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was stern and upright; when Yu Dazhong's local bandits took Xin'an they seized Shan and forced him to carry grain.

sentences.zh: 叱曰：「我天朝百性，肯為賊負米邪！

translations.literal: He shouted, I am a subject of the celestial dynasty—would I carry grain for bandits!
translations.idiomatic: He shouted, "I am a subject of the celestial dynasty—would I carry grain for bandits?"

sentences.zh: 」大罵而死。

translations.literal: He cursed them loudly and died.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 登英亦以罵賊死。

translations.literal: Dengying also died cursing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Dengying likewise died after reviling the bandits.

sentences.zh: 君合幼孤，母苦節，孝養惟謹。

translations.literal: Junhe was orphaned young; his mother endured in widowhood, and he supported her with scrupulous filial care.
translations.idiomatic: Junhe lost his father in childhood; his mother lived in chaste widowhood, and he supported her with scrupulous filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 賊至，聚眾保沙岸寨。

translations.literal: When bandits came, he gathered the people to defend Sha'an Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came he rallied the people to hold Sha'an Stockade.

sentences.zh: 攻圍十晝夜不克，說之降，大罵不從。

translations.literal: They besieged it for ten days and nights without success, urged him to surrender, but he cursed them and refused.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days and nights of siege they could not take it; when they urged him to surrender he cursed them and refused.

sentences.zh: 寨破，被磔。

translations.literal: When the stockade fell he was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: When the stockade fell he was dismembered alive.

sentences.zh: 我正素豪俠，集眾保鄉里，一方賴之。

translations.literal: Wozheng had long been bold and chivalrous; he gathered men to protect the countryside, and the whole area relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wozheng had long been bold and chivalrous; he gathered men to defend the countryside, and the whole region relied on him.

sentences.zh: 十四年勒眾禦賊，馘三人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he led the people against bandits and severed three heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he led the people against the bandits and cut off three heads.

sentences.zh: 俄賊大至，眾悉奔，奮臂獨戰。

translations.literal: Soon a great host of bandits came; everyone fled, but he fought alone with bared arms.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a great bandit force arrived; everyone fled, but he fought on alone.

sentences.zh: 賊愛其男，欲生致之，詬罵自刎死。

translations.literal: The bandits admired his valor and wished to take him alive; he reviled them and cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits admired his courage and wished to take him alive; he reviled them and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 我德知賊至，恐妻子受辱，驅一家二十七人登樓自焚。

translations.literal: Wode, learning that bandits had come, fearing dishonor for his wife and children, drove twenty-seven members of his household upstairs and burned themselves together.
translations.idiomatic: Wode, learning that bandits were coming and fearing dishonor for his wife and children, led twenty-seven members of his household upstairs and burned themselves together.

sentences.zh: 挺生精星術，預卜十五年有寇禍，編茅河渚以居。

translations.literal: Tingsheng was skilled in astrology and foretold calamity from raiders fifteen years ahead; he built a thatched hut on a river islet to live in.
translations.idiomatic: Tingsheng was skilled in astrology and foretold raiders fifteen years in advance; he built a thatched hut on a river islet and lived there.

sentences.zh: 賊蹤跡得之，語其妻梁氏曰：「此匹夫徇義之秋也。

translations.literal: When bandits tracked him down, he told his wife Lady Liang, This is the season for a plain man to die for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits tracked him down he told his wife, Lady Liang, "This is the moment for an ordinary man to die for righteousness."

sentences.zh: 」夫婦對泣，詬賊而死。

translations.literal: Husband and wife wept facing each other, cursed the bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife wept face to face, cursed the bandits, and died.

sentences.zh: 世濟與兄世舟並為土寇於大中所執，將殺之。

translations.literal: Shiji and his elder brother Shizhou were both seized by Yu Dazhong's local bandits and were about to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji and his elder brother Shizhou were both seized by Yu Dazhong's local bandits and were about to be executed.

sentences.zh: 兄弟相抱泣，賊議釋其一，世濟即奪賊刀自殺，世舟獲免。

translations.literal: The brothers embraced weeping; the bandits debated releasing one of them, whereupon Shiji seized a bandit's knife and killed himself, and Shizhou was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers embraced and wept; when the bandits debated releasing one of them, Shiji seized a bandit's knife and killed himself, and Shizhou was spared.

sentences.zh: 佩玉者，御史興元孫也。

translations.literal: Peiyu was the grandson of Censor Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Peiyu was the grandson of Censor Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，中州盡殘，佩玉結遺民捍鄉井，與鄰寨相掎角，往往尾賊後，奪其輜重。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen the central provinces were ravaged; Peiyu rallied surviving people to defend the villages, coordinated with neighboring stockades, and often followed behind bandits to seize their baggage trains.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Chongzhen the central provinces lay in ruins; Peiyu rallied survivors to defend the villages, coordinated with neighboring stockades, and often trailed the bandits to seize their baggage trains.

sentences.zh: 賊憚之，不敢出其境。

translations.literal: The bandits feared him and dared not venture out of his territory.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits feared him and dared not leave his territory.

sentences.zh: 後大舉圍別寨，佩玉往救，力戰而死，裏人聚哭之。

translations.literal: Later when they besieged another stockade in force, Peiyu went to its relief, fought to the death, and the townspeople gathered to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the bandits besieged another stockade in force, Peiyu went to its relief, fought to the death, and the townspeople gathered to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 時寵有孝行。

translations.literal: Shichong was known for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 賊陷城，其父宗祀以年老不能行，命之速避，遂自殺。

translations.literal: When bandits took the city, his father Zongsi, too old to flee, ordered him to escape quickly and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits took the city, his father Zongsi, too old to flee, urged him to escape at once and then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 時寵慟哭，刺殺一子、三女，夫婦並自剄。

translations.literal: Shichong wept bitterly, stabbed one son and three daughters, and he and his wife both cut their throats.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong wept in anguish, stabbed one son and three daughters, and he and his wife cut their throats together.

sentences.zh: 其妹適歸寧，亦從死，一家死者八人。

translations.literal: His sister, visiting home on marriage leave, died with them; eight in the family perished.
translations.idiomatic: His sister, who had come home on a visit, died with them as well; eight members of the family perished.

sentences.zh: 方國儒，字道醇，歙縣人。

translations.literal: Fang Guoru, courtesy name Daochun, was a native of She county.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guoru, whose courtesy name was Daochun, came from She county.

sentences.zh: 四歲失父，奉母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He lost his father at four and was famed for supporting his mother in filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at the age of four and became known for supporting his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he passed the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi he passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 崇禎間，授保康知縣。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he was appointed magistrate of Baokang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he was appointed magistrate of Baokang.

sentences.zh: 流賊大入湖廣，將吏率望風先奔。

translations.literal: When roving bandits poured into Huguang, commanders and officials for the most part fled at the mere rumor.
translations.idiomatic: When roving bandits poured into Huguang, commanders and officials for the most part fled at the first rumor of their approach.

sentences.zh: 保康小邑素無兵，七年正月賊至，國儒急率鄉兵出禦，力不支，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Baokang was a small district long without troops; in the first month of the seventh year bandits arrived, and Guoru urgently led militia out to resist; when his strength failed the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Baokang was a small district with scarcely any troops; in the first month of the seventh year the bandits arrived, and Guoru hastily led the militia out to resist, but when his strength failed the city fell.

sentences.zh: 亡何，賊退，國儒還入城。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits withdrew and Guoru re-entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the bandits withdrew, and Guoru returned to the city.

sentences.zh: 逾月復至，督吏民固拒。

translations.literal: A month later they returned and he urged officials and people to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: A month later they returned, and he urged officials and townspeople to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 賊至益眾，復陷。

translations.literal: The bandits came in greater numbers and the city fell again.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits came in greater numbers, and the city fell again.

sentences.zh: 國儒官服坐堂上，被執大罵，身中七刃死。

translations.literal: Guoru sat on the dais in official robes, was seized, cursed them loudly, and died after seven blade wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Guoru sat on the dais in his official robes; seized by the bandits, he cursed them loudly and died after seven blade wounds.

sentences.zh: 賊陷竹谿，訓導王紹正死之。

translations.literal: When bandits took Zhuxi, Instructor Wang Shaozheng died defending it.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits took Zhuxi, Instructor Wang Shaozheng died in its defense.

sentences.zh: 谷城舉人常存畏會試赴京，道遇賊，欲劫為首領，罵不絕口死。

translations.literal: Gucheng licentiate Chang Cunwei, traveling to the capital for the metropolitan examination, met bandits on the road who wished to make him their leader; he cursed them without cease and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Cunwei, a licentiate of Gucheng traveling to the capital for the metropolitan examination, met bandits on the road who wished to make him their leader; he cursed them without cease and was killed.

sentences.zh: 他賊犯興山，知縣劉定國堅守。

translations.literal: Other bandits attacked Xingshan; Magistrate Liu Dingguo held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Other bandits attacked Xingshan, and Magistrate Liu Dingguo held the city firm.

sentences.zh: 城將陷，遣吏懷印送上官，罵賊死。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall he sent an official bearing the seal to the superior authorities and died cursing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall he sent an official bearing the seal to his superiors and died cursing the bandits.

sentences.zh: 何承光，貴州鎮遠人。

translations.literal: He Chengguang was a native of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengguang came from Zhenyuan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Wanli he passed the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year of Wanli he passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，歷夔州同知。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he served in turn as Assistant Prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he served as Assistant Prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，賊由荊州入夔門，犯夔州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year bandits entered through Jingzhou and the Kuimen, attacking Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year the bandits entered through Jingzhou and the Kuimen and attacked Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 副使周士登在涪州，城中倉猝無備，通判、推官、知縣悉遁。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Zhou Shideng was at Fuzhou; the city was suddenly unprepared, and the subprefect, investigating censor, and magistrate all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Zhou Shideng was at Fuzhou; the city was caught unprepared, and the subprefect, investigating censor, and magistrate all fled.

sentences.zh: 承光攝府事，率吏民固守，力竭城陷。

translations.literal: Chengguang acted in charge of the prefecture, led officials and people in a stubborn defense, and when strength failed the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Chengguang took charge of the prefecture, led officials and townspeople in a stubborn defense, and when their strength failed the city fell.

sentences.zh: 承光整冠帶危坐，賊入殺之，投屍於江。

translations.literal: Chengguang straightened his hat and sash and sat upright; when bandits entered they killed him and cast his body into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Chengguang straightened his hat and sash and sat upright; when the bandits entered they killed him and cast his body into the river.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈承光夔州知府。

translations.literal: When reported, Chengguang was posthumously made Prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Chengguang was posthumously appointed Prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 自賊起陜西，轉寇山西、畿輔、河南、北及湖廣、四川，陷州縣以數十許，未有破大郡者，至是天下為震動。

translations.literal: Since the bandits rose in Shaanxi and turned to raid Shanxi, the capital region, Henan, then north to Huguang and Sichuan, they had taken dozens of prefectures and districts but not yet breached a great commandery—now the whole realm was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Since the bandits had risen in Shaanxi and turned to raid Shanxi, the capital region, Henan, and then Huguang and Sichuan, they had taken dozens of prefectures and districts but had not yet breached a major commandery—now the whole realm was shaken.

sentences.zh: 其他部自漢中犯大寧，知縣高日臨見勢弱不能守，嚙指書牒乞援上官，率眾禦之北門。

translations.literal: Another band entered from Hanzhong against Daning; Magistrate Gao Rilin, seeing the force too weak to hold, bit his finger and wrote a dispatch begging aid from superiors, then led the people to defend the North Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Another band entered from Hanzhong against Daning; Magistrate Gao Rilin, seeing that the force was too weak to hold the city, bit his finger and wrote a dispatch begging aid from his superiors, then led the people to defend the North Gate.

sentences.zh: 兵敗被執，大罵不屈，賊碎其體焚之。

translations.literal: Defeated and seized, he cursed them and would not yield; the bandits shattered his body and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated and captured, he cursed them and refused to submit; the bandits shattered his body and burned it.

sentences.zh: 訓導高錫及妻女，巡檢陳國俊及妻，皆遇害。

translations.literal: Instructor Gao Xi and his wife and daughters, Patrol Inspector Chen Guojun and his wife, all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Gao Xi and his wife and daughters, and Patrol Inspector Chen Guojun and his wife, all perished.

sentences.zh: 日臨，字儼若，鄱陽恩貢生。

translations.literal: Rilin, courtesy name Yanruo, was a favored tribute student from Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rilin, whose courtesy name was Yanruo, was a favored tribute student from Poyang.

sentences.zh: 賊陷夔州，他賊即以次日陷巫山，通江巡檢郭纘化陣沒，通江指揮王永年力戰死。

translations.literal: When bandits took Kuizhou, others on the very next day took Wushan; Tongjiang Patrol Inspector Guo Xuanhua fell in battle, and Tongjiang Commander Wang Yongnian died fighting to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits took Kuizhou, another band took Wushan the very next day; Tongjiang Patrol Inspector Guo Xuanhua fell in battle, and Tongjiang Commander Wang Yongnian died fighting to the end.

sentences.zh: 至四月，守備郭震辰、指揮田實擊賊百丈關，兵敗被執，罵賊死。

translations.literal: By the fourth month Garrison Commander Guo Zhenchen and Commander Tian Shi attacked bandits at Baizhang Pass; defeated and seized, they died cursing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth month Garrison Commander Guo Zhenchen and Commander Tian Shi attacked the bandits at Baizhang Pass; defeated and captured, they died cursing the bandits.

sentences.zh: 龐瑜，字堅白，公安人。

translations.literal: Pang Yu, courtesy name Jianbai, was a native of Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Yu, whose courtesy name was Jianbai, came from Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 家貧，躬耕自給。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he farmed with his own hands to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and he supported himself by farming with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 夏轉水灌田，執書從牛後，朗誦不輟。

translations.literal: In summer when the turning water irrigated the fields, he held his book behind the ox and recited aloud without pause.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, when the turning water irrigated the fields, he would walk behind the ox with a book in hand, reciting aloud without pause.

sentences.zh: 由歲貢生授京山訓導。

translations.literal: Through the annual tribute student route he was appointed Instructor of Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Through the annual tribute-student route he was appointed Instructor of Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年擢陜西崇信知縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he was promoted to Magistrate of Chongxin in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he was promoted to magistrate of Chongxin in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 縣無城，兵荒，貧民止百余戶。

translations.literal: The district had no wall, was ravaged by war, and had barely more than a hundred poor households.
translations.idiomatic: The district had no city wall, had been ravaged by war, and had barely more than a hundred poor households.

sentences.zh: 瑜知賊必至，言於監司陸夢龍，以無兵辭。

translations.literal: Yu knew bandits were sure to come and told Supervising Secretary Lu Menglong, declining on grounds of no troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yu knew the bandits were sure to come and told Supervising Secretary Lu Menglong, declining the post on grounds that he had no troops.

sentences.zh: 瑜集士民築土垣以守，流涕誓死職。

translations.literal: Yu gathered gentry and people to build an earthen rampart for defense, weeping as he swore to die at his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gathered gentry and townspeople to build an earthen rampart for defense, weeping as he swore to die at his post.

sentences.zh: 閏八月天大雨，土垣盡圮。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month heaven sent great rain and the earthen ramparts collapsed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month heavy rains fell, and the earthen ramparts collapsed entirely.

sentences.zh: 賊掩至，瑜急解印遣家人賫送上官，端坐堂上以待。

translations.literal: Bandits rushed up; Yu quickly unsealed the seal and sent his family to deliver it to superiors, then sat upright on the dais to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits rushed up; Yu quickly removed the seal and sent his family to deliver it to his superiors, then sat upright on the dais to await them.

sentences.zh: 賊至，捽令跪。

translations.literal: When bandits arrived they dragged him down and ordered him to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits arrived they dragged him down and ordered him to kneel.

sentences.zh: 瑜罵曰：「賊奴敢辱官長！

translations.literal: Yu cursed them, How dare you bandit slaves insult a superior official!
translations.idiomatic: Yu cursed them, "How dare you bandit slaves insult a superior official!"

sentences.zh: 」拔刀脅之，罵益厲。

translations.literal: They drew blades to threaten him and he cursed all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: They drew their blades to threaten him, and he cursed them all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 賊掠城中無所有，執至野外，剖心裂屍而去。

translations.literal: Finding nothing worth looting in the city, they took him to the open country, cut out his heart, dismembered his corpse, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Finding nothing worth looting in the city, they took him into the open country, cut out his heart, dismembered his corpse, and left.

sentences.zh: 贈固原知州。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Prefect of Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed prefect of Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 時賊盡趨秦中，長吏多殉城者。

translations.literal: By then the bandits were all rushing into Qinzhong and many chief officials died with their cities.
translations.idiomatic: By then the bandits were all rushing into Qinzhong, and many chief officials died with their cities.

sentences.zh: 山陽陷，知縣董三謨，黎平舉人也，及父嗣成、弟三元俱死之，妻李氏亦攜子女偕死。

translations.literal: When Shanyang fell, Magistrate Dong Sanmo, a licentiate from Liping, died together with his father Sicheng and younger brother Sanyuan; his wife Lady Li also took her children and died with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanyang fell, Magistrate Dong Sanmo, a licentiate from Liping, died together with his father Sicheng and younger brother Sanyuan; his wife, Lady Li, also took her children and died with them.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿丞，立祠，與嗣成、三元並祀，妻女建坊旌表。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; a shrine was erected and he was worshiped together with Sicheng and Sanyuan; his wife and daughters were honored with an arch.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; a shrine was erected in which he was worshiped together with Sicheng and Sanyuan; his wife and daughters were honored with a commemorative arch.

sentences.zh: 吉永祚，輝縣人。

translations.literal: Ji Yongzuo was a native of Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yongzuo came from Huixian.

sentences.zh: 為鳳縣主簿，謝事將歸。

translations.literal: He served as Registrar of Feng county and was about to resign and return home.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as registrar of Feng county and was about to resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 會賊至，知縣棄城遁，永祚倡義拒守。

translations.literal: When bandits came the magistrate abandoned the city and fled; Yongzuo took the lead in organizing defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came the magistrate abandoned the city and fled; Yongzuo took the lead in organizing the defense.

sentences.zh: 城陷，北面再拜曰：「臣雖小吏，嘗食祿於朝，不敢以謝事逃責。

translations.literal: When the city fell he bowed twice to the north and said, Though I am a humble clerk, I have eaten the state's grain and dare not evade duty because I have resigned.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he bowed twice to the north and said, "Though I am only a humble clerk, I have eaten the state's grain and dare not evade my duty because I have resigned."

sentences.zh: 」大罵死之。

translations.literal: He cursed them loudly and died.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 子士樞、士模皆死。

translations.literal: His sons Shishu and Shimo both died.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shishu and Shimo both died.

sentences.zh: 教諭李之蔚、鄉官魏炳亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Instructor Li Zhiwei and local official Wei Bing also refused to yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Li Zhiwei and local official Wei Bing likewise refused to submit and were killed.

sentences.zh: 永祚贈漢中衛經歷，余贈恤有差。

translations.literal: Yongzuo was posthumously made Administrator of the Hanzhong guard; the others received graded posthumous honors and relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzuo was posthumously made administrator of the Hanzhong guard; the others received posthumous honors and relief in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 婁琇知涇州。

translations.literal: Lou Xiu was magistrate of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xiu was magistrate of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏八月，城陷死，贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month the city fell and he died; he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month the city fell and he died; he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 蒲來舉知甘泉。

translations.literal: Pu Laiju was magistrate of Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Laiju was magistrate of Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 賊來犯，守備孫守法等擁兵不救。

translations.literal: When bandits came to attack, Garrison Commander Sun Shoufa and others held troops back and did not relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came to attack, Garrison Commander Sun Shoufa and others held their troops back and did not come to the city's relief.

sentences.zh: 城破，來舉手刃一賊，傷六賊而後死。

translations.literal: When the city fell Laiju with his own hand killed one bandit and wounded six before he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Laiju killed one bandit with his own hand and wounded six others before he died.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 呂鳴世，福建人。

translations.literal: Lü Mingshi was a native of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mingshi was from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由恩貢生為麟遊知縣。

translations.literal: Through the grace-enrolled tribute student route he became magistrate of Linyou.
translations.idiomatic: By way of the grace-enrolled tribute student route, he was appointed magistrate of Linyou.

sentences.zh: 兵燹後，拊居民有恩。

translations.literal: After the ravages of war he comforted the residents with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: After the devastation of war, he treated the townspeople with such kindness that they owed him a debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊不忍加害，自絕食六日卒。

translations.literal: When the city fell the bandits could not bear to harm him; he starved himself for six days and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the bandits could not bring themselves to harm him; he refused food for six days until he died.

sentences.zh: 有宋緒湯者，耀州諸生，被獲，大罵死。

translations.literal: There was one Song Xutang, a Yaozhou student, who was captured and died after cursing them loudly.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Song Xutang, a student from Yaozhou, who was captured and met death hurling curses at the bandits.

sentences.zh: 尹夢鰲，雲南太和人。

translations.literal: Yin Meng'ao was a native of Taihe in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Meng'ao was from Taihe in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中知潁州。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he served as prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he served as prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年正月方謁上官於鳳陽，聞流賊大至，立馳還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he was just paying respects to his superior at Fengyang when he heard that roving bandits were coming in force; he immediately galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year he was in Fengyang paying his respects to a superior when word came that a great force of roving bandits was approaching; he turned his horse at once and raced back.

sentences.zh: 賊已抵城下，乃偕通判趙士寬率民固守。

translations.literal: The bandits had already reached the foot of the city wall, so together with Assistant Prefect Zhao Shikuan he led the people in a stout defense.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were already at the city walls. He joined Assistant Prefect Zhao Shikuan in leading the people in a desperate defense.

sentences.zh: 城北有高樓間城中，諸生劉廷傳請先據之，夢鰲以為然。

translations.literal: North of the city there was a tall tower overlooking the interior; student Liu Tingchuan asked to seize it first, and Meng'ao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city stood a tall tower that commanded the ground within the walls. Liu Tingchuan, a local student, urged that they seize it first, and Meng'ao agreed.

sentences.zh: 而廷傳所統皆市人，不可用。

translations.literal: But those under Tingchuan's command were all townspeople and could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: But the men Tingchuan commanded were townspeople, not soldiers, and proved useless.

sentences.zh: 賊遂據樓以攻，且鑿城，頹數丈，城上人皆走，止之不可。

translations.literal: The bandits then seized the tower to attack, and also dug at the wall until several zhang collapsed; those on the wall all fled, and could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits took the tower and attacked from it, while also undermining the wall until a stretch several zhang long gave way. The defenders on the ramparts broke and fled, and nothing could hold them back.

sentences.zh: 夢鰲持大刀，獨當城壞處，殺賊十余人，身被數刃。

translations.literal: Meng'ao took up a great sword and alone blocked the breach, killing more than ten bandits while receiving several wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'ao seized a broadsword and alone held the breach, killing more than ten bandits before he himself was cut several times.

sentences.zh: 賊眾畢登，遂投城下烏龍潭死，弟侄七人皆死之。

translations.literal: When the bandits had all climbed in, he threw himself into Wulongtan below the city wall and died; seven younger brothers and nephews also died with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits had swarmed over the walls, he cast himself into the Black Dragon Pool below the city and died. Seven younger brothers and nephews died with him.

sentences.zh: 廷傳者，故布政使九光從子，任俠好義，亦罵賊死。

translations.literal: Tingchuan was the nephew of the former provincial administration commissioner Jiuguang; chivalrous and fond of righteousness, he too cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tingchuan was the nephew of the former provincial administration commissioner Jiuguang, a man given to chivalry and righteous conduct; he too died cursing the bandits.

sentences.zh: 九光子廷石分守西城，中賊刃未絕，口授友人方略，令繕牘上當事，旋卒。

translations.literal: Jiuguang's son Tingshi separately defended the west wall; struck by bandit blades but not yet dead, he orally dictated strategy to a friend and had a memorial drafted for the authorities, then soon expired.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuguang's son Tingshi held the west wall. Though cut down by the bandits, he had not yet breathed his last; he dictated a plan of action to a friend and had a memorial written up for the authorities, then died.

sentences.zh: 士寬，字汝良，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Shikuan, styled Ruliang, was a native of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: Shikuan, styled Ruliang, was from Ye County.

sentences.zh: 由門蔭為鳳陽通判，駐潁州。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he became assistant prefect of Fengyang, stationed at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he was appointed assistant prefect of Fengyang and stationed at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以正旦詣郡城，聞警，一日夜馳三百里返州。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day he went to the prefectural city; hearing the alarm, he rode three hundred li back to the prefecture in a day and a night.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day he had gone to the prefectural seat; when he heard the alarm, he rode three hundred li back to Yingzhou in a single day and night.

sentences.zh: 城陷，率家眾巷戰，力竭，亦投烏龍潭死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he led his household in street fighting until strength was exhausted, then also threw himself into Wulongtan and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he led his household in fighting through the alleys until his strength was spent, then cast himself into the Black Dragon Pool and died.

sentences.zh: 妻李攜三女登樓自焚，仆王丹亦罵賊死。

translations.literal: His wife Li took their three daughters up a tower and burned themselves; the servant Wang Dan also cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Li took their three daughters up a tower and burned themselves to death. The servant Wang Dan likewise died cursing the bandits.

sentences.zh: 鄉官尚書張鶴鳴、弟副使鶴勝、子大同，中書舍人田之穎，知縣劉道遠，光祿署正李生白，訓導丁嘉遇，舉人郭三傑，諸生韓光祿等，皆死之。

translations.literal: Local officials including Minister Zhang Heming, his younger brother Vice Commissioner Heming, and his son Datong; Secretariat Drafter Tian Zhiying; Magistrate Liu Daoyuan; Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Li Shengbai; Instructor Ding Jiayu; Provincial Graduate Guo Sanjie; student Han Guanglu and others—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Among the local officials who died were Minister Zhang Heming, his younger brother Vice Commissioner Heming, and his son Datong; Secretariat Drafter Tian Zhiying; Magistrate Liu Daoyuan; Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Li Shengbai; Instructor Ding Jiayu; provincial graduate Guo Sanjie; the student Han Guanglu; and many others.

sentences.zh: 光祖，進士獻策父也，被執，賊捽使跪。

translations.literal: Guangzu, father of the jinshi Xianc, was seized; the bandits dragged him and forced him to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu, father of the jinshi Xianc, was captured. The bandits dragged him down and forced him to his knees.

sentences.zh: 叱曰：「吾生平讀書，止知忠義。

translations.literal: He shouted, All my life of reading books I have known only loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted, "All my years of reading have taught me one thing only: loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 」遂大罵。

translations.literal: Then he cursed them loudly.
translations.idiomatic: " He then hurled abuse at them.

sentences.zh: 賊殺之，碎其屍。

translations.literal: The bandits killed him and hacked his corpse to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits killed him and hacked his body to pieces.

sentences.zh: 妻武偕一妹、一女並獻策妻李赴井死。

translations.literal: His wife Wu, together with one younger sister and one daughter, along with Xianc's wife Li, threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Wu, together with a younger sister and a daughter, along with Xianc's wife Li, threw themselves down a well and died.

sentences.zh: 妾李方有娠，賊剖腹剔胎死。

translations.literal: Concubine Li was just pregnant; the bandits cut open her belly, removed the fetus, and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine Li was pregnant. The bandits cut open her belly, tore out the unborn child, and killed her.

sentences.zh: 次子定策、孫日曦罵賊死，獨獻策獲存。

translations.literal: The second son Dingce and grandson Rixi cursed the bandits and died; only Xianc survived.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Dingce and the grandson Rixi died cursing the bandits. Only Xianc survived.

sentences.zh: 時被難者共一百三人，城中婦人死節者三十七人，烈女八人。

translations.literal: At that time those who perished in the calamity numbered one hundred and three in all; within the city thirty-seven women died preserving their chastity, and eight were celebrated as heroic women.
translations.idiomatic: In all, one hundred and three people perished in the disaster. Thirty-seven women in the city died defending their honor, and eight were counted among the heroic women.

sentences.zh: 潁州忠烈，稱獨盛雲。

translations.literal: The loyal martyrs of Yingzhou were said to have been uniquely abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal martyrs of Yingzhou were said to have been unmatched in number.

sentences.zh: 潁州衛隸河南，流賊至，指揮李從師、王廷俊，千戶孫升、田三震，百戶羅元慶、田得民、王之麟俱乘城戰死。

translations.literal: The Yingzhou Guard was subordinate to Henan; when roving bandits arrived, Commanders Li Congshi and Wang Tingjun, Battalion Commanders Sun Sheng and Tian Sanzhen, and Company Commanders Luo Yuanqing, Tian Demin, and Wang Zhilin all mounted the walls and died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingzhou Guard was under Henan's jurisdiction. When the roving bandits arrived, Commanders Li Congshi and Wang Tingjun, Battalion Commanders Sun Sheng and Tian Sanzhen, and Company Commanders Luo Yuanqing, Tian Demin, and Wang Zhilin all took to the walls and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 賊既陷潁州，屠其民。

translations.literal: After the bandits had taken Yingzhou, they slaughtered its people.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yingzhou had fallen, the bandits massacred its people.

sentences.zh: 其別部即以是月由壽州犯鳳陽。

translations.literal: A separate division of theirs that same month advanced from Shouzhou against Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: That same month a separate band of theirs marched from Shouzhou against Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽故無城，中都留守朱國相率指揮袁瑞徵、呂承蔭、郭希聖、張鵬翼、周時望、李郁、嶽光祚，千戶陳弘祖、陳其忠、金龍化等，以兵三千逆賊上窯山，多斬獲。

translations.literal: Fengyang originally had no city wall. Garrison Commander of the Central Capital Zhu Guoxiang led Commanders Yuan Ruizheng, Lü Chengyin, Guo Xisheng, Zhang Pengyi, Zhou Shiwang, Li Yu, and Yue Guangzuo, and Battalion Commanders Chen Hongzu, Chen Qizhong, Jin Longhua, and others, with three thousand troops to meet the bandits at Shangyaoshan, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang had never had city walls. Zhu Guoxiang, garrison commander of the Central Capital, led Commanders Yuan Ruizheng, Lü Chengyin, Guo Xisheng, Zhang Pengyi, Zhou Shiwang, Li Yu, and Yue Guangzuo, together with Battalion Commanders Chen Hongzu, Chen Qizhong, Jin Longhua, and others, and with three thousand troops intercepted the bandits at Shangyaoshan, killing and capturing many of them.

sentences.zh: 俄賊數萬至，矢集如猬，遂敗，國相自刎死，余皆陣沒。

translations.literal: Soon tens of thousands of bandits arrived; arrows gathered thick as a hedgehog, and they were defeated. Guoxiang cut his own throat and died; the rest all fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Before long tens of thousands of bandits arrived, and arrows fell so thick they bristled like a hedgehog. The defenders were routed. Guoxiang cut his own throat and died; the rest were killed on the field.

sentences.zh: 賊遂犯皇陵，大肆焚掠。

translations.literal: The bandits then violated the imperial tombs and burned and plundered on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then descended on the imperial tombs and burned and plundered without restraint.

sentences.zh: 知府顏容暄囚服匿於獄，釋囚獲之，容暄大罵，賊杖殺之。

translations.literal: Prefect Yan Rongxuan, in prison garb, hid himself in the jail; released prisoners seized him. Rongxuan cursed them loudly, and the bandits beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yan Rongxuan, dressed in prison garb, had hidden himself in the jail. Freed prisoners found him. Rongxuan cursed them loudly, and the bandits beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 血浸石階，宛如其像，滌之不滅。

translations.literal: Blood soaked the stone steps, exactly like his likeness; washed, it would not fade.
translations.idiomatic: His blood soaked the stone steps in a shape exactly like his likeness, and no amount of washing could make it fade.

sentences.zh: 士民乃取石立冢，建祠奉祀。

translations.literal: The gentry and commoners then took stone and raised a tomb, built a shrine, and offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The local gentry and townspeople then erected a stone tomb for him, built a shrine, and made offerings in his honor.

sentences.zh: 推官萬文英臥病，賊索之。

translations.literal: Magistrate's Assistant Wan Wenying lay ill; the bandits searched for him.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate's Assistant Wan Wenying was bedridden with illness, and the bandits came looking for him.

sentences.zh: 子元亨，年十六，泣語父曰：「兒不得復事親矣！

translations.literal: His son Yuanheng, sixteen years old, wept and said to his father, I can no longer serve you as a son!
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanheng, sixteen years old, wept and said to his father, "I shall never again be able to serve you as a son!

sentences.zh: 」出門呼曰：「若索官，何為？

translations.literal: Going out the door he called, If you seek the official, for what purpose?
translations.idiomatic: " He went out and cried, "If you are looking for the official, what are you waiting for?

sentences.zh: 我即官也。

translations.literal: I am the official.
translations.idiomatic: I am the official.

sentences.zh: 賊縶之。

translations.literal: The bandits seized him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits seized him.

sentences.zh: 顧見其師萬師尹亦被縶，紿賊曰：「若欲得者，官爾。

translations.literal: Looking back he saw his teacher Wan Shiyin also seized; he deceived the bandits, saying, If you want the official, here he is.
translations.idiomatic: Glancing back he saw his teacher Wan Shiyin also in bonds. He deceived the bandits, saying, "If you want the official, here he is.

sentences.zh: 何縶此賤隸？

translations.literal: Why seize this lowly servant?
translations.idiomatic: Why bind this worthless servant?

sentences.zh: 」賊遂釋之。

translations.literal: The bandits then released him.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits then released Shiyin.

sentences.zh: 元亨乃極口大罵。

translations.literal: Yuanheng then cursed them to the utmost with his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng then poured out the fiercest curses.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，斷脛死，文英獲免。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger severed his shins and killed him; Wenying was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits hacked through his legs and killed him. Wenying was spared.

sentences.zh: 容暄，漳浦人。

translations.literal: Rongxuan was a native of Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxuan was from Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 文英，南昌人。

translations.literal: Wenying was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenying was from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 皆進士。

translations.literal: Both were jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Both were jinshi.

sentences.zh: 一時同死者，千戶陳永齡、百戶盛可學等四十一人，諸生六十六人。

translations.literal: Those who died together at the same time included Battalion Commander Chen Yongling, Company Commander Sheng Kexue, and others—forty-one in all—and sixty-six students.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died at the same time included Battalion Commander Chen Yongling, Company Commander Sheng Kexue, and others—forty-one in all—as well as sixty-six students.

sentences.zh: 舉人蔣思宸聞變，投繯死。

translations.literal: Provincial Graduate Jiang Sichen, hearing of the disaster, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When provincial graduate Jiang Sichen heard what had happened, he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 後給事中林正亨錄上其狀，贈夢鰲光祿少卿，士寬光祿丞，余贈恤有差。

translations.literal: Later Supervising Secretary Lin Zhengheng recorded and submitted the account; Meng'ao was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Shikuan made Director of that court, and the rest received posthumous honors and relief according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later Supervising Secretary Lin Zhengheng submitted a full report of what had happened. Meng'ao was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Shikuan Director of that court, and the others received posthumous honors and relief according to their rank.

sentences.zh: 盧謙，字吉甫，廬江人。

translations.literal: Lu Qian, styled Jifu, was a native of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian, styled Jifu, was from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授永豐知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，出為江西右參政，引疾歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor, then sent out as Right Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi, and returned home citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor, then appointed Right Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi, but retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年二月，流賊犯廬江，士民具財帛求免，賊偽許之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits invaded Lujiang; gentry and commoners gathered wealth and silks seeking exemption, and the bandits falsely promised it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits attacked Lujiang. The gentry and townspeople gathered money and goods to buy their safety, and the bandits pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 俄襲陷其城，謙服命服，危坐中門。

translations.literal: Soon they suddenly attacked and took the city; Qian put on his official robes and sat upright at the central gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they launched a surprise attack and took the city. Qian put on his official robes and sat upright at the central gate.

sentences.zh: 賊至，欲屈之，罵曰：「吾朝廷憲臣，肯為賊屈邪？

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived and wished to humiliate him, he cursed, saying, I am a surveillance official of the court—would I bow to bandits?
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came and tried to break him, he cursed them, saying, "I am a surveillance official of the imperial court. Would I bow to bandits?

sentences.zh: 鼠輩滅亡在即，安敢無禮！

translations.literal: You vermin are on the verge of destruction—how dare you show such disrespect!
translations.idiomatic: You rats are about to be destroyed. How dare you treat me with such disrespect!

sentences.zh: 」賊怒殺之，投屍於池，池水盡赤。

translations.literal: In anger the bandits killed him and threw his corpse into a pool; the pool water turned completely red.
translations.idiomatic: " Enraged, the bandits killed him and threw his body into a pool, and the water turned completely red.

sentences.zh: 舉人張受、畢尹周亦不屈被殺。

translations.literal: Provincial Graduates Zhang Shou and Bi Yinzhou also would not submit and were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graduates Zhang Shou and Bi Yinzhou likewise refused to submit and were killed.

sentences.zh: 是年正月，賊陷霍丘，縣丞張有俊，教諭倪可大，訓導何炳，鄉官田既庭、戴廷對，舉人王毓貞死焉。

translations.literal: In the first month of that year the bandits took Huoqiu; Assistant Magistrate Zhang Youjun, Instructor Ni Ked, Instructor He Bing, local officials Tian Jiting and Dai Tingdui, and Provincial Graduate Wang Yuzhen died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of that year the bandits took Huoqiu. Assistant Magistrate Zhang Youjun, Instructor Ni Ked, Instructor He Bing, local officials Tian Jiting and Dai Tingdui, and provincial graduate Wang Yuzhen all died there.

sentences.zh: 賊陷巢縣，知縣嚴覺被執不屈，一門皆死。

translations.literal: When the bandits took Chaoxian, Magistrate Yan Jue was seized and would not submit; his whole household died.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits took Chaoxian, Magistrate Yan Jue was captured and refused to submit. His entire household perished.

sentences.zh: 二月犯太湖，知縣金應元據城東大濠以守。

translations.literal: In the second month they invaded Taihu; Magistrate Jin Yingyuan held the great moat east of the city to defend.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they attacked Taihu. Magistrate Jin Yingyuan defended the city from the great moat on the east side.

sentences.zh: 奸人導賊渡濠，執應元，斫之未殊，自經死。

translations.literal: Traitors guided the bandits across the moat; they seized Yingyuan and hacked him without killing him outright, and he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Traitors showed the bandits how to cross the moat. They seized Yingyuan and hacked at him without finishing him off, so he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 訓導扈永寧亦死之。

translations.literal: Instructor Hu Yongning also died.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Hu Yongning also died.

sentences.zh: 謙贈光祿卿，余贈恤如制。

translations.literal: Qian was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; the rest received posthumous honors and relief according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the others received posthumous honors and relief as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 覺，歸安人。

translations.literal: Jue was a native of Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jue was from Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 應元，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Yingyuan was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan was from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 皆舉人。

translations.literal: Both were provincial graduates.
translations.idiomatic: Both were provincial graduates.

sentences.zh: 龔元祥，字子禎，長洲人。

translations.literal: Gong Yuanxiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yuanxiang, styled Zizhen, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年為霍山教諭，厲廉隅，以名教自任，與訓導姚允恭友善。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he became instructor of Huoshan; strict in integrity, he took upon himself the charge of moral teaching, and was on friendly terms with Instructor Yao Yungong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was appointed instructor of Huoshan. Stern in his personal integrity and devoted to the moral teachings of the sages, he became close friends with Instructor Yao Yungong.

sentences.zh: 八年，賊陷鳳陽，元祥偕縣令守禦。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when bandits took Fengyang, Yuanxiang together with the county magistrate defended.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the bandits took Fengyang, Yuanxiang joined the county magistrate in organizing the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊掩至，令逸去，元祥督士民固守。

translations.literal: The bandits arrived by surprise; the magistrate fled, and Yuanxiang supervised gentry and commoners in a stout defense.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits struck without warning. The magistrate fled, but Yuanxiang rallied the gentry and townspeople and held the city.

sentences.zh: 或勸之避，元祥曰：「食祿而避難，不忠。

translations.literal: Some urged him to flee; Yuanxiang said, To receive salary and flee from danger is disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to flee. Yuanxiang said, "To draw an official salary and then run from danger is disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 臨危而棄城，不義。

translations.literal: To face peril and abandon the city is unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: To face danger and abandon the city is unrighteousness.

sentences.zh: 吾平日講說者謂何？

translations.literal: What then have my daily lectures been about?
translations.idiomatic: What, then, have all my daily lectures been about?

sentences.zh: 倘不測，死爾。

translations.literal: If the unexpected comes, then death, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: If the worst should come, then I die—that is all.

sentences.zh: 」及賊陷城，元祥整衣冠危坐。

translations.literal: When the bandits took the city, Yuanxiang straightened his cap and robes and sat upright.
translations.idiomatic: " When the bandits broke into the city, Yuanxiang straightened his cap and robes and sat waiting in formal posture.

sentences.zh: 賊至，侃侃諭以大義。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, he calmly expounded the great principles to them.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came, he addressed them calmly and at length on the principles of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 賊欲屈之，厲聲曰：「死即死，賊輩何敢辱我！

translations.literal: When the bandits wished to humiliate him, he said in a fierce voice, Die then die—how dare you bandits insult me!
translations.idiomatic: When they tried to break him, he cried in a thunderous voice, "Then let me die! How dare you bandits insult me!

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，執之去，罵不絕口，遂遇害。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger seized him and took him away; he cursed without cease and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Enraged, the bandits seized him and dragged him away. He never stopped cursing, and so he was killed.

sentences.zh: 子炳衡號呼罵賊，賊又殺之。

translations.literal: His son Bingheng cried out and cursed the bandits; the bandits killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bingheng shouted curses at the bandits, and they killed him as well.

sentences.zh: 閱五日，允恭斂其屍，即自縊，適令至，解免。

translations.literal: After five days Yungong gathered his corpse, then hanged himself; just then an order arrived and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Yungong recovered the body and then tried to hang himself, but an order happened to arrive just then granting relief, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 越日，賊復入，允恭卒死之。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits entered again, and Yungong finally died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the bandits returned, and Yungong died at last.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈元祥國子助教，建祠曰忠孝，以其子配。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Yuanxiang was posthumously made Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education; a shrine called Loyalty and Filial Piety was built, with his son enshrined beside him.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Yuanxiang was posthumously made Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education. A shrine called Loyalty and Filial Piety was built, with his son enshrined beside him.

sentences.zh: 允恭亦被旌。

translations.literal: Yungong also received official commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong was also officially commended.

sentences.zh: 王信，陜西寧州人。

translations.literal: Wang Xin was a native of Ningzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin was from Ningzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父歿，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: When his father died, he lived by the tomb for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he lived beside the tomb in mourning for three years.

sentences.zh: 母歿，信年已六十，足不逾閾者三年。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Xin was already sixty, yet for three years his feet did not cross the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Xin was already sixty years old, yet for three years he did not step beyond his threshold.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，由歲貢生除靈璧訓導，遷真陽知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, through the annual tribute student route he was appointed instructor of Lingbi, then transferred to magistrate of Zhenyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign, by way of the annual tribute student route, he was appointed instructor of Lingbi and later transferred to magistrate of Zhenyang.

sentences.zh: 八年二月出撫土寇，會流賊猝至，被執，使諭降羅山、真陽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he went out to pacify local bandits; roving bandits suddenly arrived, he was seized, and they made him urge the surrender of Luoshan and Zhenyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he went out to pacify local bandits. Roving bandits suddenly appeared, seized him, and forced him to go and persuade Luoshan and Zhenyang to surrender.

sentences.zh: 信大罵不從，斷頭剖腹而死。

translations.literal: Xin cursed them loudly and would not obey; they severed his head and cut open his belly, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xin cursed them and refused. They cut off his head, disemboweled him, and left him dead.

sentences.zh: 閱四日，其子來覓，猶舒指握子手。

translations.literal: After four days his son came looking for him; he still extended his fingers and grasped his son's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Four days later his son came searching for him and found that his fingers were still relaxed enough to clasp his son's hand.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿丞，建祠奉祀。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; a shrine was built and sacrifices were offered to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and a shrine was erected for his worship.

sentences.zh: 史記言，字司直，當塗人。

translations.literal: Shi Jiyan, styled Sizhi, was a native of Dangtu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jiyan, styled Sizhi, was from Dangtu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中舉人，由長沙知縣遷知陜州。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he became a provincial graduate; from magistrate of Changsha he was transferred to prefect of Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he passed the provincial examinations and served as magistrate of Changsha before being transferred to prefect of Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陜當賊沖，記言出私財募士，聘少室僧訓練之。

translations.literal: Shaan lay in the bandits' path; Jiyan spent his private funds to recruit soldiers and hired Shaoshi monks to train them.
translations.idiomatic: Shaan Prefecture lay directly in the bandits' path. Jiyan spent his own money to raise troops and hired monks from Shaoshi to drill them.

sentences.zh: 八年冬十一月，流賊犯陜，記言禦之，斬數十級，生擒二十余人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the winter of the eighth year roving bandits attacked Shaan; Jiyan resisted them, beheaded several dozen, and captured more than twenty alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eighth year roving bandits attacked Shaan. Jiyan drove them back, beheaded several dozen, and took more than twenty prisoners.

sentences.zh: 老回回憤，率數萬人攻城，不克，乘雪夜來襲，而所練士方調他郡，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Lao Huihui was enraged; he led tens of thousands to attack the city but could not take it. Taking advantage of a snowy night he came in a surprise attack, while the trained troops had just been transferred to another prefecture, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Lao Huihui led tens of thousands to storm the city but failed. He returned on a snowy night and caught the defenders off guard just as Jiyan's trained troops had been sent to another prefecture, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 記言縱火自焚，兩僧掖之出曰：「死此，何以自明？

translations.literal: Jiyan set fire to burn himself to death; two monks pulled him out and said, "If you die here, how will you clear your name?
translations.idiomatic: Jiyan tried to burn himself to death, but two monks pulled him out and said, "If you die here, how will you prove your innocence?

sentences.zh: 」乃越女墻下。

translations.literal: " Then they helped him over the parapet.
translations.idiomatic: " They then helped him over the city wall.

sentences.zh: 賊追獲之，令降，叱曰：「有死知州，無降知州也！

translations.literal: The bandits pursued and captured him and ordered him to surrender. He shouted, "There is a dead prefect, but no surrendered prefect!
translations.idiomatic: The bandits caught up with him and ordered him to surrender. He shouted back, "There is a dead prefect, but no prefect who surrenders!

sentences.zh: 」遂被殺。

translations.literal: " Then he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Then they killed him.

sentences.zh: 指揮李君賜殺數賊而死。

translations.literal: Commander Li Junci killed several bandits and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Junci killed several bandits before he himself was killed.

sentences.zh: 訓導王誠心，裏居教諭張敏行、姚良弼，指揮楊道泰、阮我疆，鎮撫陳三元，亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Instructor Wang Chengxin, retired instructors Zhang Minxing and Yao Liangbi, commanders Yang Daotai and Ruan Wojiang, and garrison adjutant Chen Sanyuan also refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Wang Chengxin, retired instructors Zhang Minxing and Yao Liangbi, commanders Yang Daotai and Ruan Wojiang, and garrison adjutant Chen Sanyuan likewise refused to yield and were killed.

sentences.zh: 是月，賊陷盧氏，知縣白楹自剄。

translations.literal: That month the bandits took Lushi; Magistrate Bai Ying cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the bandits captured Lushi, and Magistrate Bai Ying slit his own throat.

sentences.zh: 十年九月陷澠池，知縣李邁林死之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the tenth year they took Mianchi; Magistrate Li Mailin died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the tenth year they captured Mianchi, and Magistrate Li Mailin died defending it.

sentences.zh: 記言贈光祿少卿，余贈恤有差。

translations.literal: Jiyan was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; the others received posthumous honors and relief in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyan was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the others received posthumous honors and relief according to rank.

sentences.zh: 梁誌仁，南京人，保定侯銘之裔也。

translations.literal: Liang Zhiren was a native of Nanjing and a descendant of Marquis Baoding Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhiren was from Nanjing and a descendant of Marquis Baoding Ming.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年授衡陽知縣，調羅田。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he was appointed magistrate of Hengyang and was transferred to Luotian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he was appointed magistrate of Hengyang and later transferred to Luotian.

sentences.zh: 賊大擾湖廣，誌仁日夕儆備。

translations.literal: Bandits greatly ravaged Huguang; Zhiren remained on alert day and night.
translations.idiomatic: As bandits ravaged Huguang, Zhiren kept the county on constant alert day and night.

sentences.zh: 羅汝才謂左右曰：「羅田城小易克，然梁君長者，吾不忍加兵。

translations.literal: Luo Rucai said to those around him, "Luotian's walls are small and easy to take, but Magistrate Liang is a worthy man; I cannot bear to send troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Rucai told his followers, "Luotian is a small city and easy to capture, but Magistrate Liang is a man of virtue, and I cannot bring myself to attack him.

sentences.zh: 俟其去，當取之。

translations.literal: Wait until he leaves, and then we shall take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until he is gone, and then we will take it.

sentences.zh: 」會邑豪江猶龍與賊通，誌仁捕下獄。
