translations.literal: " It happened that local magnate Jiang Youlong was in contact with the bandits; Zhiren arrested him and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " Meanwhile a local power broker named Jiang Youlong was colluding with the bandits, and Zhiren had him arrested and thrown in jail.

sentences.zh: 猶龍知必死，潛導汝才別校來攻。

translations.literal: Youlong knew he would surely die, so he secretly guided one of Rucai's subordinate commanders to come and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he faced certain execution, Youlong secretly led one of Rucai's subordinate commanders to attack the city.

sentences.zh: 八年二月猝攻城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year they suddenly attacked the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year they launched a sudden assault on the city.

sentences.zh: 誌仁急偕典史單思仁、教諭吳鳳來、訓導盧大受督民守禦。

translations.literal: Zhiren hurriedly joined with county clerk Shan Siren, instructor Wu Fenglai, and instructor Lu Dashou to lead the people in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren rushed to join County Clerk Shan Siren, Instructor Wu Fenglai, and Instructor Lu Dashou in organizing the people's defense.

sentences.zh: 城陷，誌仁持長矛巷戰，殺六賊。

translations.literal: The city fell; Zhiren fought in the alleys with a long spear and killed six bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Zhiren fought through the streets with a long spear and killed six bandits.

sentences.zh: 力屈被縶，抑使跪。

translations.literal: His strength gave out and he was bound; they forced him to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Exhausted, he was seized and forced to his knees.

sentences.zh: 罵曰：「我天子命官，肯屈膝賊輩邪！

translations.literal: He cursed them, saying, "I am an officer appointed by the Son of Heaven—would I bow my knees to bandits like you!
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them, saying, "I am an officer appointed by the Son of Heaven—do you think I would kneel before bandits like you!

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，碎其支體，焚之。

translations.literal: " The bandits were enraged; they shattered his limbs and burned him.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits flew into a rage, smashed his body to pieces, and burned him.

sentences.zh: 妻唐被逼，大罵，奪賊刀不得，口嚙賊手，遂遇害。

translations.literal: His wife Tang was pressed hard; she cursed loudly, tried to seize a bandit's knife but could not, bit the bandit's hand with her mouth, and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Tang, was seized and cursed the bandits fiercely. Unable to wrest a knife from them, she bit a bandit's hand and was killed.

sentences.zh: 思仁等亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Siren and the others also refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Siren and the others likewise refused to yield and were killed.

sentences.zh: 汝才在英山，聞之，馳至羅田，斬其別校，曰：「奈何擅害長者！

translations.literal: Rucai was in Yingshan; when he heard of it he galloped to Luotian, beheaded that subordinate commander, and said, "How dare you harm a worthy man on your own authority!
translations.idiomatic: Rucai was in Yingshan at the time. When he heard what had happened, he rode to Luotian, executed the subordinate commander, and said, "How dare you kill a worthy man without my orders!

sentences.zh: 」以錦繡斂其夫婦屍。

translations.literal: " He had the corpses of the husband and wife wrapped in brocade for burial.
translations.idiomatic: " He had the couple's bodies wrapped in brocade for burial.

sentences.zh: 鳳來，福建舉人。

translations.literal: Fenglai was a provincial graduate from Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Fenglai was a provincial graduate from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 大受，寶慶貢生。

translations.literal: Dashou was a tribute student from Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou was a tribute student from Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 詔贈誌仁蘄州知州，思仁羅田主簿，鳳來國子助教，大受學錄，蔭子，祭葬有差。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made Zhiren Prefect of Qizhou, Siren Registrar of Luotian, Fenglai Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education, and Dashou Recorder of the Directorate of Education; sons were granted yin privilege, and state sacrifices and burial were granted according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously appointed Zhiren prefect of Qizhou, Siren registrar of Luotian, Fenglai Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education, and Dashou Recorder of the Directorate of Education. Their sons received yin privilege, and state sacrifices and burial were granted according to rank.

sentences.zh: 王國訓，字振之，解州人。

translations.literal: Wang Guoxun, styled Zhenzhi, was a native of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guoxun, styled Zhenzhi, was from Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a presented scholar in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 歷知金鄉、壽張、滋陽、武清。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Jinxiang, Shouzhang, Ziyang, and Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Jinxiang, Shouzhang, Ziyang, and Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 坐大計，久之，補調扶風。

translations.literal: He failed the triennial evaluation; after a long while he was reassigned to Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: After failing the triennial evaluation, he waited a long time before being reassigned to Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 國訓性剛嚴，恥幹進，故官久不遷。

translations.literal: Guoxun's nature was stern and severe; he was ashamed of currying favor for advancement, and so for a long time his office was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxun was stern and upright by nature and scorned the arts of self-advancement, so for many years he received no promotion.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年秋，賊來犯，偕主簿夏建忠、典史陳紹南、教諭張弘綱、訓導陳繻嬰城固守。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year of Chongzhen bandits came to attack; together with registrar Xia Jianzhong, county clerk Chen Shaonan, instructor Zhang Honggang, and instructor Chen Xu he defended the city stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year of Chongzhen, when bandits attacked, he joined Registrar Xia Jianzhong, County Clerk Chen Shaonan, Instructor Zhang Honggang, and Instructor Chen Xu in a stubborn defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 閱兩月，外援不至，城陷，罵賊死。

translations.literal: After two months outside relief did not arrive; the city fell, and he cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: After two months with no relief from outside, the city fell. He cursed the bandits and was killed.

sentences.zh: 建忠等亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Jianzhong and the others also refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong and the others likewise refused to yield and were killed.

sentences.zh: 贈國訓光祿少卿，建忠等皆贈恤。

translations.literal: Guoxun was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Jianzhong and the others all received posthumous honors and relief.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxun was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Jianzhong and the others all received posthumous honors and relief.

sentences.zh: 當是時，大帥曹文詔、艾萬年等並戰歿，賊勢益張，關中諸州縣悉殘破。

translations.literal: At that time the great commanders Cao Wenzhao, Ai Wannian, and others all died in battle; the bandits' power grew ever greater, and the prefectures and counties of Guanzhong were all ravaged.
translations.idiomatic: By then the great commanders Cao Wenzhao, Ai Wannian, and others had all fallen in battle. The bandits grew ever stronger, and the prefectures and counties of Guanzhong lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊陷永壽，殺知縣薄匡宇。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the bandits took Yongshou and killed Magistrate Bo Kuangyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the bandits captured Yongshou and killed Magistrate Bo Kuangyu.

sentences.zh: 尋陷咸陽，殺知縣趙躋昌。

translations.literal: Soon after they took Xianyang and killed Magistrate Zhao Jichang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they captured Xianyang and killed Magistrate Zhao Jichang.

sentences.zh: 其時長吏以死聞者，隴州知州胡爾純，自經死。

translations.literal: Among the senior officials reported to have died at that time was Prefect Hu Erchun of Longzhou, who hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Among the senior officials who died at that time was Hu Erchun, prefect of Longzhou, who hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 延長知縣萬代芳與教諭譚恩、驛丞羅文魁協力守城，城陷皆死之。

translations.literal: Magistrate Wan Daifang of Yanchang, together with Instructor Tan En and post-station assistant Luo Wenkuai, joined forces to defend the city; when the city fell they all died.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Wan Daifang of Yanchang, Instructor Tan En, and Post-station Assistant Luo Wenkuai worked together to hold the city, and all died when it fell.

sentences.zh: 代芳妻劉、妾梁從死。

translations.literal: Daifang's wife Liu and concubine Liang followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Daifang's wife, Lady Liu, and his concubine, Lady Liang, died with him.

sentences.zh: 爾純，山東人，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Erchun was a native of Shandong and was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Erchun was from Shandong and was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 代芳贈光祿丞，妻妾建坊旌表。

translations.literal: Daifang was posthumously made Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his wife and concubine were honored with a memorial arch.
translations.idiomatic: Daifang was posthumously appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and his wife and concubine were honored with a memorial arch.

sentences.zh: 恩等亦賜祭。

translations.literal: En and the others also received grants of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: En and the others also received grants of state sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 有孫仲嗣者，膚施人，由貢生為階州學正。

translations.literal: There was Sun Zhongsi, a native of Fushi, who through the tribute student route became director of studies of Jie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: There was Sun Zhongsi of Fushi, who entered service as a tribute student and became director of studies at Jie Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 當事知其才，委以城守。

translations.literal: Those in charge knew his ability and entrusted him with defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities recognized his ability and put him in charge of the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 賊大至，盡瘁死守。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived in force, he exhausted himself in steadfast defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came in force, he threw himself into a desperate defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 城破，與妻子十余人並死之。

translations.literal: When the city was broken, he and more than ten members of his family, wife and children included, all died together.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he died together with his wife, children, and more than ten members of his household.

sentences.zh: 贈國子博士。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Doctor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Doctor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 又有楊呈秀，華陰人。

translations.literal: There was also Yang Chengxiu, a native of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Yang Chengxiu of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 由進士歷官順慶知府，大計罷歸。

translations.literal: Through the jinshi route he served as prefect of Shunqing; after failing the triennial evaluation he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi degree holder, he had served as prefect of Shunqing before being dismissed after the triennial evaluation and sent home.

sentences.zh: 賊攻城，佐有司禦賊以死，贈恤如制。

translations.literal: When bandits attacked the city he assisted the officials in resisting the bandits and died; posthumous honors and relief were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits besieged the city he aided the local officials in the defense and was killed. He received posthumous honors and relief according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 黎弘業，字孟擴，順德人。

translations.literal: Li Hongye, styled Mengkuo, was a native of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongye, styled Mengkuo, was from Shunde.

sentences.zh: 由舉人知和州。

translations.literal: Through the provincial graduate route he became magistrate of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate, he was appointed magistrate of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年，流賊犯和州，禦卻之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongzhen roving bandits attacked He Prefecture; he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits attacked He Prefecture, and he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 十二月復至，與鄉官馬如蛟募死士，登陴固守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they returned; together with local official Ma Rujiao he recruited men willing to die, mounted the battlements, and defended steadfastly.
translations.idiomatic: They returned in the twelfth month. Together with local official Ma Rujiao he recruited volunteers, manned the battlements, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 城將陷，弘業系印於肘，跪告其母曰：「兒不肖，貪微官以累母，奈何！

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall, Hongye tied his seal to his elbow, knelt, and told his mother, "Your son is unworthy; I coveted a petty office and have brought trouble upon you—what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall, Hongye tied his official seal to his arm, knelt before his mother, and said, "I am an unworthy son. I clung to a petty office and have brought disaster upon you—what can be done!

sentences.zh: 」母李泣諭曰：「汝勿以我為意，事至此，有死而已。

translations.literal: " His mother Li wept and instructed him, saying, "Do not consider me; matters have come to this—there is only death.
translations.idiomatic: " His mother, Lady Li, wept and told him, "Do not worry about me. It has come to this, and there is nothing left but death.

sentences.zh: 」遂自縊。

translations.literal: " Then she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " Then she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 妻楊、妾李及女四人繼之。

translations.literal: His wife Yang, concubine Li, and four daughters followed her.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Yang, his concubine, Lady Li, and four daughters followed her in death.

sentences.zh: 弘業北面慟哭再拜，自刎未殊，濡頸血大書曰：「為臣盡忠，為子盡孝，何惜一死。

translations.literal: Hongye turned to the north, wept bitterly, and bowed twice; he cut his own throat but did not die immediately, smeared blood on his neck, and wrote in large characters, "As a minister fulfill loyalty, as a son fulfill filial piety—what is one death to regret?
translations.idiomatic: Hongye turned north, wept, and bowed twice. He slashed his own throat but did not die at once. Smearing blood across his neck, he wrote in large characters, "A minister owes loyalty; a son owes filial piety—why regret a single death?

sentences.zh: 」賊入，傷數刃而死。

translations.literal: " When the bandits entered, he was wounded by several blades and died.
translations.idiomatic: " When the bandits entered the city, they cut him down with several blades and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太仆少卿，任一子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and one son was appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and one son was granted an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 判官錢大用偕妻妾子婦俱死。

translations.literal: Judge Qian Dayong died together with his wife, concubines, and daughters-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Qian Dayong died together with his wife, concubines, and daughters-in-law.

sentences.zh: 吏目景一高被創死。

translations.literal: Clerk Jing Yigao was wounded and died.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Jing Yigao was wounded and killed.

sentences.zh: 學正康正諫，祁門人，舉人。

translations.literal: Director of Studies Kang Zhengjian was a native of Qimen and a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Studies Kang Zhengjian was from Qimen and a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 偕妻汪、子婦章赴水死，贈國子監丞。

translations.literal: Together with his wife Wang and daughter-in-law Zhang he entered the water and died; he was posthumously made Assistant Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned himself together with his wife, Lady Wang, and his daughter-in-law, Lady Zhang, and was posthumously appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 訓導趙世選不屈死，贈國子學錄。

translations.literal: Instructor Zhao Shixuan refused to submit and died; he was posthumously made Recorder of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Zhao Shixuan refused to yield and was killed; he was posthumously appointed Recorder of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 馬如蛟，字騰仲，州人。

translations.literal: Ma Rujiao, styled Tengzhong, was a native of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rujiao, styled Tengzhong, was a native of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a presented scholar in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 授浙江山陰知縣，有清操。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Shanyin in Zhejiang and had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Shanyin in Zhejiang and was known for his upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年征授御史，劾罷魏忠賢黨徐紹吉、張訥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed censor; he impeached and had dismissed Xu Shaoji and Zhang Ne, members of Wei Zhongxian's faction.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned to serve as a censor and impeached Xu Shaoji and Zhang Ne, allies of Wei Zhongxian, leading to their dismissal.

sentences.zh: 出按四川，蜀中奸民悉以他人田產投勢家，如蛟列上十事，永革其弊。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect Sichuan; in Shu wicked commoners all transferred others' land and property to powerful families. Rujiao submitted a list of ten matters and permanently abolished that abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to inspect Sichuan, he found that unscrupulous locals were transferring other people's land and property to powerful families. Rujiao submitted ten reform proposals and permanently abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 還朝，監武會試。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he supervised the military metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he supervised the military metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 武舉董姓者，以技勇聞於帝，及入試，文不中程，被黜。

translations.literal: A military licentiate surnamed Dong, famed to the emperor for skill and valor, entered the examination but failed the literary portion and was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: A military licentiate surnamed Dong, whose skill and bravery were well known to the emperor, took the examination but failed the literary portion and was disqualified.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，黜考官，如蛟亦落職。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; the examiners were dismissed, and Rujiao also lost his office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. The examiners were dismissed, and Rujiao lost his post as well.

sentences.zh: 八年論平邦彥功，復故官，以父憂未赴。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when merit in pacifying Bangyan was assessed, his former office was restored, but because of mourning for his father he did not take up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his former post was restored in recognition of the campaign against Bangyan, but he was still in mourning for his father and did not take it up.

sentences.zh: 流賊至，如蛟傾貲募士，佐弘業固守。

translations.literal: When roving bandits arrived, Rujiao spent all his resources to recruit soldiers and assisted Hongye in steadfast defense.
translations.idiomatic: When roving bandits arrived, Rujiao spent his entire fortune to raise troops and helped Hongye hold the city.

sentences.zh: 麾壯士出擊，兩戰皆捷。

translations.literal: He commanded brave men to sally forth in attack; in two battles they were both victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He led picked fighters out in counterattack and won both engagements.

sentences.zh: 賊將奔，會風雪大作，不辨人色，守者皆潰，賊遂入城。

translations.literal: The bandits were about to flee when suddenly a great wind and snow arose; people could not tell one another apart, the defenders all broke and fled, and the bandits then entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were on the verge of retreat when a blizzard struck. In the whiteout the defenders could not tell friend from foe, the garrison collapsed, and the bandits poured into the city.

sentences.zh: 如蛟急下令，能擊賊者，予百金，須臾得百余人。

translations.literal: Rujiao urgently issued an order: whoever could strike the bandits would receive a hundred taels of gold; in a moment he gathered more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Rujiao urgently offered a hundred taels of gold to anyone who would fight the bandits, and within moments more than a hundred men rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 巷戰，賊多傷，力屈，遂戰死。

translations.literal: They fought in the alleys; many bandits were wounded; his strength gave out, and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They fought through the streets, wounding many bandits, but their strength failed and Rujiao fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 兄鹽運司判官如虬、諸生如虹及家屬十四人皆死。

translations.literal: His elder brother Rujiu, a judge of the Salt Transport Commission, the student Ruhong, and fourteen members of the household all died.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Rujiu, a judge on the Salt Transport Commission, his brother Ruhong, a student, and fourteen members of their household all died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太仆少卿，官一子。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and one son was appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and one son was granted an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 張紹登，字振夫，南城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shaodeng, styled Zhenfu, was a native of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shaodeng, styled Zhenfu, was from Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中舉人，知應城縣。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he became a provincial graduate and served as magistrate of Yingcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he passed the provincial examinations and served as magistrate of Yingcheng.

sentences.zh: 九年，賊來犯，偕訓導張國勛、鄉官饒可久悉力禦之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year bandits came to attack; together with Instructor Zhang Guoxun and local official Rao Kejiu he exerted all his strength to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when bandits attacked, he joined Instructor Zhang Guoxun and local official Rao Kejiu in an all-out defense.

sentences.zh: 國勛曰：「賊不一創，城不易守。

translations.literal: Guoxun said, "If the bandits are not struck a blow, the city will not be easy to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxun said, "Unless we give the bandits a hard blow, this city will not hold.

sentences.zh: 」率壯士出擊，力戰一日夜，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: " He led brave men out in attack; they fought fiercely for a day and a night and beheaded and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: " He led picked fighters out in a sortie. They fought fiercely for a day and a night, killing and capturing a great many bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊去，邑侍郎王瑊之子權結怨於族黨，怨家潛導賊復來攻。

translations.literal: The bandits departed. Quan, son of Wang Jian, assistant director of the district, had incurred the enmity of his clansmen, and his enemies secretly guided the bandits back to attack again.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits withdrew, Quan, son of the district assistant director Wang Jian, had fallen out with members of his clan, and his enemies secretly led the bandits back for another assault.

sentences.zh: 國勛佐紹登力守，而乞援於上官。

translations.literal: Guoxun assisted Shaodeng in defending with all his strength and begged aid from his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxun aided Shaodeng in a stout defense and sent pleas for reinforcements to the authorities above.

sentences.zh: 副將鄧祖禹來救，守西南，國勛守東北，紹登往來策應。

translations.literal: Vice general Deng Zuyu came to the rescue; he held the southwest, Guoxun held the northeast, and Shaodeng moved back and forth to coordinate the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Vice general Deng Zuyu arrived to relieve the city. He held the southwest wall, Guoxun held the northeast, and Shaodeng shuttled between them directing the response.

sentences.zh: 會賊射書索權，權懼，斬北關以出，賊乘間登南城。

translations.literal: When the bandits shot in a letter demanding Quan, Quan grew afraid, cut through the north gate to flee, and the bandits seized the opportunity to scale the south wall.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then shot a message into the city demanding Quan. Terrified, Quan hacked open the north gate and fled, and the bandits took advantage of the breach to climb onto the south wall.

sentences.zh: 紹登還署，端坐堂上，賊至，奮拳擊之。

translations.literal: Shaodeng returned to his office, sat upright in the hall, and when the bandits arrived he struck them with his fists.
translations.idiomatic: Shaodeng went back to the yamen, seated himself upright in the main hall, and when the bandits burst in he fought them bare-handed.

sentences.zh: 群賊大至，乃被殺。

translations.literal: When a great mass of bandits arrived, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits swarmed in, they cut him down.

sentences.zh: 賊渠嘆其忠，以冠帶覆屍，埋堂側。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain sighed at his loyalty, covered the corpse with cap and sash, and buried it beside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leader marveled at his loyalty, draped his body with official cap and sash, and buried him beside the hall.

sentences.zh: 國勛，黃陂歲貢生。

translations.literal: Guoxun was a tribute student from Huangpi.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxun had been a tribute student from Huangpi.

sentences.zh: 賊既入，朝服北面拜，走捧先聖神主，拱立以待。

translations.literal: After the bandits had entered, he put on court dress, bowed facing north, ran to take up the spirit tablets of the ancient sages, and stood with hands clasped waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Once the bandits were inside, he donned his court robes, bowed toward the north, ran to gather up the spirit tablets of the sages, and stood holding them with clasped hands, awaiting death.

sentences.zh: 賊遂焚文廟，投國勛於烈焰中。

translations.literal: The bandits then burned the Confucian temple and cast Guoxun into the flames.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then set fire to the Confucian temple and threw Guoxun into the blaze.

sentences.zh: 祖禹亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Zuyu also died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu likewise refused to yield and was killed.

sentences.zh: 可久，幼孤，事母孝，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Kejiu, orphaned in youth, served his mother filially and passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Kejiu lost his father young, served his mother with filial devotion, and passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 知大興縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Daxing County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Daxing County.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，疏請更《三朝要典》，時奄宦擅權，謫光祿典簿。

translations.literal: In the early Chongzhen reign he memorialized requesting revision of the Records of Three Reigns Essentials; at the time eunuchs monopolized power, and he was demoted to records clerk in the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he submitted a memorial calling for revision of the Records of Three Reigns Essentials. Eunuchs then held sway at court, and he was demoted to records clerk in the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 遷應天府推官、刑部主事，歷知府，丁艱歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to investigating censor of Yingtian Prefecture and secretary in the Ministry of Justice, served as prefect, and returned home on mourning leave for a parent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor of Yingtian and secretary in the Ministry of Justice, later served as prefect, and returned home to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 賊入，語妻程曰：「臣死忠，婦死節，分也。

translations.literal: When the bandits entered, he said to his wife Cheng, "A minister dies in loyalty; a wife dies in chastity — that is our allotted lot.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits broke in, he told his wife Cheng, "It is a minister's part to die loyal, and a wife's part to die chaste.

sentences.zh: 」於是妻女相對自經。

translations.literal: " Thereupon his wife and daughter faced each other and hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: " His wife and daughter then faced each other and hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 可久被執，賊強之拜，曰：「頭可斷，膝不可屈也！

translations.literal: Kejiu was seized; the bandits forced him to bow. He said, "The head may be cut off, but the knees cannot bend!
translations.idiomatic: Kejiu was captured and the bandits tried to force him to kowtow. He declared, "You may take my head, but you will never bend my knees!

sentences.zh: 」遂遇害。

translations.literal: " He was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then put to death.

sentences.zh: 瑊為賊支解。

translations.literal: Jian was dismembered by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was hacked to pieces by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈紹登尚寶少卿，國勛國子學正。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Shaodeng was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals and Guoxun Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Shaodeng was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals and Guoxun Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 王燾，字浚仲，昆山人。

translations.literal: Wang Tao, styled Junzhong, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tao, styled Junzhong, was from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，九歲為人後。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, at the age of nine he became another family's heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was orphaned and destitute as a boy, and at nine he was made the heir of another family.

sentences.zh: 族人有謀其產者，燾舉以讓之，迎養嗣祖母及母惟謹。

translations.literal: When a clansman plotted to seize his property, Tao offered it all to him and welcomed and supported his adoptive grandmother and mother with the utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: When a kinsman tried to seize his inheritance, Tao yielded the whole estate to him and devoted himself to caring for his adoptive grandmother and mother.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末，舉於鄉，由教諭歷隨州知州。

translations.literal: Late in the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination and rose from instructor to magistrate of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examinations and advanced from county instructor to prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 州經群盜焚掠，戶不滿千。

translations.literal: The prefecture had been ravaged by bandits; households numbered fewer than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had been laid waste by roving bandits, and fewer than a thousand households remained.

sentences.zh: 燾訓民兵，繕守具。

translations.literal: Tao trained the militia and repaired the defensive equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Tao drilled the militia and restored the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 土寇李良喬為亂，殲滅之。

translations.literal: The local bandit Li Liangqiao raised a rebellion, and Tao exterminated him.
translations.idiomatic: When the local bandit Li Liangqiao rebelled, Tao wiped out his force.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，大賊奄至。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, a great bandit force suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year, a major rebel army suddenly appeared.

sentences.zh: 燾且守且戰，擊斬三百余人。

translations.literal: Tao both defended and fought, killing more than three hundred in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Tao held the city while fighting back, killing more than three hundred of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊攻益力，相持二十余日。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed their attack more fiercely, and the two sides remained locked in combat for more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits redoubled their assault, and the siege dragged on for more than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 天大風雪，守者多散。

translations.literal: Heaven sent a great wind and snow, and many of the defenders scattered.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce blizzard struck, and many defenders broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 燾知必敗，入署，整冠帶自經。

translations.literal: Tao knew defeat was inevitable, entered his office, straightened his cap and sash, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that defeat was inevitable, Tao went into the yamen, adjusted his cap and sash, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 賊焚其署，火燭不及燾死所，屍直立不仆，賊望見駭走。

translations.literal: The bandits burned his office, but the flames did not reach the place where Tao died; his corpse stood upright without falling, and when the bandits saw it they fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits torched the yamen, but the fire never reached the spot where Tao had died. His body remained standing upright, and the bandits who saw it fled in horror.

sentences.zh: 已，覓州印，得之燾所立尺士下。

translations.literal: Later, when they searched for the prefectural seal, they found it beneath about a chi of earth at the place where Tao had stood.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, when the prefectural seal was sought, it was found buried under about a foot of earth where Tao had been standing.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 福王時，賜謚烈湣，建雙忠祠，與同邑蔡懋德並祀。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, he was granted the posthumous name Lie Min, a Double Loyalty Shrine was built, and he was worshipped together with Cai Maode of the same county.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was granted the posthumous name Lie Min, a shrine to both loyal men was erected, and he was enshrined together with his fellow townsman Cai Maode.

sentences.zh: 有魏時光者，南昌人。

translations.literal: There was one Wei Shiguang, a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Wei Shiguang, from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 善舞雙刀。

translations.literal: He was skilled at wielding twin sabers.
translations.idiomatic: He was expert with paired sabers.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年夏，為廣濟典史。

translations.literal: In the summer of the ninth year of Chongzhen he served as registrar of Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Chongzhen 9 he was appointed registrar of Guangji.

sentences.zh: 邑遭殘破，長吏設排兵三百人，委之教練。

translations.literal: The county had been devastated; the chief officials established a standing force of three hundred men and entrusted their training to him.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay in ruins, so the senior officials raised a standing force of three hundred men and put him in charge of drilling them.

sentences.zh: 其冬，賊據蘄州河口，憚時光不敢渡。

translations.literal: That winter the bandits held the river mouth at Qizhou; they feared Shiguang and dared not cross.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the bandits occupied the Qizhou river crossing but feared Shiguang and would not attempt to ford the river.

sentences.zh: 時光益募死士，夜襲其營，手殺數賊，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: Shiguang recruited more dare-to-die fighters, raided their camp by night, personally killed several bandits, and the bandits dared not press him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiguang raised more volunteers willing to die fighting, struck their camp by night, killed several bandits with his own hand, and kept the enemy at bay.

sentences.zh: 俄賊大至，部卒皆散，時光單騎據高坡，又殺數人。

translations.literal: Soon a great bandit force arrived; his troops all scattered. Shiguang alone on horseback held a high slope and killed several more men.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a large rebel force arrived and his men melted away. Shiguang held a hill alone on horseback and cut down several more enemies.

sentences.zh: 賊環繞之，靷斷被執，不屈死。

translations.literal: The bandits surrounded him; his rein broke and he was seized, but he died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits closed in around him. His bridle snapped, he was captured, and he died refusing to yield.

sentences.zh: 其兄陳於上官，卻不奏。

translations.literal: His elder brother reported the matter to the superior authorities, but it was not memorialized to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother reported the affair to the local authorities, but no memorial was sent up to the throne.

sentences.zh: 兄憤發病死，友人收殮之，哭盡哀，曰：「弟為國死，兄為弟死，吾獨不能表暴之乎！

translations.literal: The elder brother died of indignant illness. A friend gathered his remains and wept with full grief, saying, "My younger brother died for the state; I die for my brother — can I alone fail to bring his deed to light!
translations.idiomatic: The elder brother died of grief and rage. A friend prepared his body for burial and wept over him, saying, "My brother died for the country, and I die for my brother — am I the only one who cannot see his sacrifice made known?

sentences.zh: 」具牘力陳，乃奏聞。

translations.literal: " He prepared a written statement setting forth the case with force, and only then was it reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " He drafted a detailed petition and pressed the case until at last it reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 贈廣濟主簿，予恤典。

translations.literal: Shiguang was posthumously made assistant director of Guangji and granted condolence honors.
translations.idiomatic: Shiguang was posthumously appointed assistant director of Guangji and granted the usual honors for the dead.

sentences.zh: 蔣佳徵，灌陽人。

translations.literal: Jiang Jiazheng was a native of Guanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jiazheng was from Guanyang.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations in the fourth year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，知盱眙縣，有聲。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he served as magistrate of Xuyi and won a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he served as magistrate of Xuyi and earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 縣故無城，佳徵知賊必至，訓民為兵。

translations.literal: The county originally had no wall. Jiazheng knew the bandits would surely come and trained the people as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The county had never had city walls. Jiazheng knew the bandits were bound to come and drilled the populace as militia.

sentences.zh: 十年秋，賊果來犯，設伏要害，親率兵往誘，賊殲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year the bandits came to attack as expected. He set ambushes at critical points, personally led troops out to lure them, and destroyed a great many bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the tenth year the bandits attacked as he had foreseen. He laid ambushes at key points, personally led men out to draw them in, and wiped out a large part of the enemy force.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，環攻之，力戰死。

translations.literal: Enraged, the bandits surrounded and attacked him, and he died fighting to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, enraged, closed in from all sides, and he fell fighting to the last.

sentences.zh: 母聞之，亦投繯死。

translations.literal: When his mother heard of it, she too hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news, his mother hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 兵部議贈奉訓大夫、尚寶少卿。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated posthumously awarding him Instructor Grand Master and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War recommended posthumously appointing him Instructor Grand Master and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals.

sentences.zh: 未幾，巡按御史言佳徵子忠母義，宜賜謚蔭，以植倫常。

translations.literal: Before long the touring censor memorialized that Jiazheng had shown filial loyalty and his mother righteous conduct, and that a posthumous name and hereditary privilege should be granted to uphold moral norms.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the touring censor argued that Jiazheng's filial devotion and his mother's moral courage deserved a posthumous title and hereditary honors, so as to uphold the bonds of human duty.

sentences.zh: 乃建表忠祠，並母奉祀。

translations.literal: Thereupon a Manifest Loyalty Shrine was built, and his mother was worshipped together with him.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine to manifest loyalty was then erected, and his mother was enshrined there with him.

sentences.zh: 同時江北死難者，有吳暢春。

translations.literal: Among those who died martyrs in Jiangbei at the same time was Wu Changchun.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who died in the line of duty in Jiangbei at the same time was Wu Changchun.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年為潛山天堂寨巡檢，練鄉兵防賊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongzhen he served as inspector of Tiantangzhai in Qianshan and trained local militia to guard against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 8 he was posted as inspector at Tiantangzhai in Qianshan, where he drilled local militia to repel bandits.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，賊至，夜設燎，大驚去之。

translations.literal: The next winter, when the bandits came, he set watch fires by night and greatly alarmed them so that they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter, when bandits approached, he lit beacon fires by night and frightened them into retreat.

sentences.zh: 逾年，賊再至，暢春死守，力屈，仰天嘆曰：「吾得死所矣！

translations.literal: After another year the bandits came again. Changchun defended to the death; when his strength was exhausted he sighed to heaven, saying, "I have found the place where I may die!
translations.idiomatic: A year later the bandits returned. Changchun held out to the end, and when his strength failed he looked up to heaven and cried, "At last I have found the place to die!

sentences.zh: 」手刃數賊，被執不屈死。

translations.literal: " He personally killed several bandits, was seized, and died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: " He cut down several bandits with his own hand, was captured, and died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 贈迪功郎、安慶府經歷，蔭子所鎮撫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Progression-of-Merit Gentleman and experience officer of Anqing Prefecture, and his son was granted hereditary appointment as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Progression-of-Merit Gentleman and experience officer of Anqing Prefecture, and his son received hereditary appointment as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 又有王寅，錢塘人。

translations.literal: There was also Wang Yin, a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wang Yin, from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 膂力絕人，舉武鄉試，以父征播功為千戶。

translations.literal: His physical strength was unmatched. He passed the military provincial examination and, by virtue of his father's merit in the Bozhou campaign, became a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Possessed of extraordinary strength, he passed the military provincial examinations and, through his father's service in the Bozhou campaign, received appointment as a company commander.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，擢撫標守備。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he was promoted to garrison commander of the Fu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he was promoted to garrison commander of the Fu garrison.

sentences.zh: 見步卒脆弱，詫曰：「曩戚將軍練浙兵，聞天下，今若爾邪！

translations.literal: Seeing how weak the foot soldiers were, he exclaimed in astonishment, "In former days General Qi drilled the Zhejiang troops, and their fame resounded under heaven — and now it has come to this!
translations.idiomatic: When he saw how feeble the foot soldiers were, he cried in dismay, "General Qi once trained the Zhejiang troops to fame throughout the realm — and now they have fallen this low!

sentences.zh: 」督教之，卒始可用。

translations.literal: " He supervised their training, and only then did the troops become usable.
translations.idiomatic: " He took charge of drilling them, and the men at last became fit for battle.

sentences.zh: 十年遷龍江都司，調赴泗州護祖陵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to regional commander of Longjiang and dispatched to Sizhou to guard the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to regional commander at Longjiang and posted to Sizhou to guard the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 賊來犯，寅曰：「賊眾我寡，及其未集，可破也。

translations.literal: When bandits came to attack, Yin said, "The bandits are many and we are few; while they have not yet gathered, we can break them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits attacked, Yin said, "They outnumber us. Strike before they fully assemble, and we can defeat them.

sentences.zh: 」卷甲疾趨，至盱眙，斬其先鋒一人。

translations.literal: " He rolled up his armor and rushed swiftly forward; reaching Xuyi, he beheaded one of their vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched at forced pace to Xuyi and cut down one of the enemy vanguard.

sentences.zh: 戰自午迄申，賊來益眾，與守備陳正亨陷陣死。

translations.literal: The battle lasted from noon until the shen hour; the bandits grew ever more numerous, and he fell in the formation together with garrison commander Chen Zhengheng and died.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting ran from noon into late afternoon as ever more bandits arrived. Yin and garrison commander Chen Zhengheng were overrun in the press of battle and killed.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮國將軍、都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Yin was posthumously made Pacifying-the-State General and Assistant Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was posthumously appointed Pacifying-the-State General and Assistant Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 正亨贈昭勇將軍、指揮使。

translations.literal: Zhengheng was posthumously made Manifest-Bravery General and commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengheng was posthumously appointed Manifest-Bravery General and commander.

sentences.zh: 並官一子。

translations.literal: Both were granted official appointment to one son each.
translations.idiomatic: One son of each man was granted an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 徐尚卿，南平人。

translations.literal: Xu Shangqing was a native of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shangqing was from Nanping.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，知劍州。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations and served as magistrate of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年十月，李自成、惠登相等以數十萬眾入四川，大將侯良柱敗歿於廣元，遂攻陷昭化，知縣王時化死之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Chongzhen, Li Zicheng, Hui Dengxiang, and others entered Sichuan with a force of several hundred thousand. The great general Hou Liangzhu was defeated and killed at Guangyuan, and they then captured Zhaohua; Magistrate Wang Shihua died in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Chongzhen 10, Li Zicheng, Hui Dengxiang, and others invaded Sichuan with an army of several hundred thousand men. General Hou Liangzhu was defeated and killed at Guangyuan, after which the rebels took Zhaohua and Magistrate Wang Shihua died defending it.

sentences.zh: 尚卿知賊必至，集士民泣曰：「城必不能守，若輩速去，吾死此。

translations.literal: Shangqing knew the bandits would surely come. He gathered the gentry and common people and wept, saying, "The city surely cannot be held. You must leave at once; I will die here.
translations.idiomatic: Shangqing knew the rebels were coming. He assembled the local gentry and townspeople and, weeping, told them, "This city cannot be held. Go quickly — I will die here.

sentences.zh: 」眾泣，請偕去，尚卿不可。

translations.literal: " The crowd wept and begged to leave together with him, but Shangqing would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " The people wept and pleaded to take him with them, but Shangqing refused.

sentences.zh: 閱二日，城陷，投繯死，吏目李英俊從之。

translations.literal: After two days the city fell. He hanged himself, and the clerk Li Yingjun followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the city fell. Shangqing hanged himself, and the clerk Li Yingjun died with him.

sentences.zh: 賊遂長驅陷江油、彰明、安縣、羅江、德陽、漢州，吏民皆先遁。

translations.literal: The bandits then drove deep and captured Jiangyou, Zhangming, Anxian, Luojiang, Deyang, and Hanzhou; officials and common people all fled beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then swept through Jiangyou, Zhangming, Anxian, Luojiang, Deyang, and Hanzhou, while officials and townspeople had already fled ahead of them.

sentences.zh: 尋掠郫縣，主簿張應奇死之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they raided Pixian, and Registrar Zhang Yingqi died.
translations.idiomatic: They soon overran Pixian, where Registrar Zhang Yingqi was killed.

sentences.zh: 陷金堂，典史潘孟科死之。

translations.literal: They captured Jintang, and Registrar Pan Mengke died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jintang fell, Registrar Pan Mengke died in the defense.

sentences.zh: 是月也，賊陷州縣三十六，以死事聞者四人。

translations.literal: In that month the bandits captured thirty-six prefectures and counties, and four men were reported as having died in the performance of duty.
translations.idiomatic: That month the rebels took thirty-six prefectures and counties, and only four deaths in office were reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 事定，贈尚卿右參議，時化光祿丞，應奇按察司知事，孟科將仕郎，並賜恤典。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Shangqing was posthumously made Right Vice Commissioner, Shihua Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Yingqi Intendant's Clerk, and Mengke Entry Officer, and all were granted condolence honors.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, Shangqing was posthumously appointed Right Vice Commissioner, Shihua Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Yingqi Intendant's Clerk, and Mengke Entry Officer, and all received the usual honors for the dead.

sentences.zh: 時化，湖廣人，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: Shihua was a native of Huguang and ranked first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shihua was from Huguang and had ranked first in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 阮之鈿，字實甫，桐城諸生。

translations.literal: Ruan Zhitian, styled Shifu, was a student of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Zhitian, styled Shifu, was a licentiate from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，下詔保舉人才，同郡諭德劉若宰以之鈿應，授谷城知縣。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign an imperial decree called for the recommendation of talented men. Liu Ruozai, instructor of the same prefecture, recommended Zhitian in response, and he was appointed magistrate of Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign the throne issued an edict soliciting recommendations of able men. Liu Ruozai, instructor of the same prefecture, nominated Zhitian, who was then appointed magistrate of Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，之鈿未至，張獻忠襲陷其城，據以求撫。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, before Zhitian had arrived, Zhang Xianzhong raided and captured the city and held it while demanding pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year, before Zhitian had even taken up his post, Zhang Xianzhong stormed and seized the city and occupied it while demanding surrender on terms.

sentences.zh: 總理熊文燦許之，處其眾數萬於四郊，居民洶洶欲竄。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xiong Wen'can agreed. He quartered their force of tens of thousands in the four suburbs, and the residents grew alarmed and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xiong Wen'can agreed to the terms and encamped tens of thousands of rebels in the outskirts, while the townspeople panicked and prepared to flee.

sentences.zh: 之鈿至，盡心調劑，民稍安，乃上疏言：「獻忠虎踞邑城，其謀叵測。

translations.literal: When Zhitian arrived, he devoted himself to mediation until the people were somewhat calmed, and then memorialized, saying, "Xianzhong crouches like a tiger in the county seat; his designs cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhitian arrived, he worked tirelessly to keep order until the people regained some calm, then memorialized the throne: "Xianzhong sits like a tiger in our county seat, and his intentions are impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 所要求之地，實兵餉取道咽喉，秦、蜀交會脈絡，今皆為所據。

translations.literal: The territory he demands is in truth the throat through which military supplies pass, the vital junction where Qin and Shu meet — and all of it is now in his hands.
translations.idiomatic: The ground he demands lies on the vital route by which troops and supplies move — the strategic junction where the Qin and Shu roads meet — and he now holds it all.

sentences.zh: 奸民甘心效用，善良悉為迫脅。

translations.literal: Wicked men gladly serve him at heart, while the good are all coerced.
translations.idiomatic: The wicked willingly serve him, while honest people are all forced into compliance.

sentences.zh: 臣守土牧民之官，至無土可守，無民可牧。

translations.literal: I am an official charged with guarding the land and shepherding the people, yet I have no land to guard and no people to shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: I am an official charged with guarding the land and caring for the people, yet I have no land left to guard and no people left to govern.

sentences.zh: 庫藏殫虛，民產被奪，無賦可征。

translations.literal: The treasury is utterly empty, the people's property has been seized, and there are no taxes to levy.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is bare, the people's goods have been seized, and there is no revenue left to collect.

sentences.zh: 名雖縣令，實贅員爾。

translations.literal: In name I am county magistrate, but in fact I am no more than a supernumerary.
translations.idiomatic: I bear the title of county magistrate, but in truth I am little more than a figurehead.

sentences.zh: 乃廟堂之上專主撫議，臣愚妄謂撫剿二策可合言，未可分言，致損國威，而挫士氣。

translations.literal: Yet above in the court they exclusively advocate the policy of pacification. This humble official presumptuously holds that the two policies of pacification and suppression may be spoken of together and ought not be spoken of separately, lest national prestige be harmed and morale be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at court they insist on pacification alone. I venture to say that pacification and suppression are two sides of one policy and must not be treated as separate courses, for to do so damages the state's prestige and breaks the army's spirit.

sentences.zh: 」時不能用。

translations.literal: " At that time it could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, however, his advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 賊眾漸出野外行劫，之鈿執之以告其營將，稍置之法。

translations.literal: The bandit masses gradually went out into the wilds to rob on the roads; Zhitian seized them and reported them to their camp commanders, who mildly punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel bands increasingly ranged into the countryside to plunder. Zhitian would seize the culprits and report them to their camp officers, who meted out minor punishments under military law.

sentences.zh: 及再告，皆不應，曰：「官司不給餉耳，得餉自止。

translations.literal: When he reported again, none responded, saying, "The government offices simply do not provide rations; once they receive rations they will stop of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported them again, no one responded, saying, "The authorities simply withhold our pay. Once we are paid, the raids will stop.

sentences.zh: 」由是村民徙亡殆盡，遂掠及阛阓。

translations.literal: " From this the village people fled and were nearly all gone, and plunder extended even to the market streets.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers fled until almost none remained, and the looting soon reached the market districts of the town.

sentences.zh: 稍拒，輒挺刃相向，日有死者，一城大囂。

translations.literal: If there was the slightest resistance, they would at once draw blades against the people; each day there were dead, and the whole city was in great uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Any resistance at all was met with drawn blades; people died every day, and the entire city was thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 監軍僉事張大經奉文燦令來鎮撫，亦不能禁。

translations.literal: The supervising army vice commissioner Zhang Dajing, on Wen'can's orders, came to pacify them, but could not restrain them either.
translations.idiomatic: Army superintendent and vice commissioner Zhang Dajing was sent by Wen'can to restore order, but he too proved unable to check them.

sentences.zh: 明年，獻忠反形漸露，之鈿往說之曰：「將軍始所為甚悖，今幸得為王臣，當從軍立功，垂名竹帛。

translations.literal: The next year Xianzhong's rebellious intent gradually showed itself; Zhitian went to persuade him, saying, "General, what you did at first was greatly perverse; now you are fortunate to have become a subject of the king. You should follow the army and achieve merit, leaving your name in bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xianzhong's intent to rebel became increasingly plain. Zhitian went to remonstrate with him: "General, your earlier conduct was deeply wrong, but you are now fortunate enough to serve the throne. You should take the field, win distinction, and leave your name in the histories.

sentences.zh: 且不見劉將軍國能乎？

translations.literal: Have you not seen General Liu Guoneng?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen what became of General Liu Guoneng?

sentences.zh: 天子手詔進宮，厚賫金帛，此赤誠效也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent a personal edict summoning him to court and richly bestowed gold and silk — this was loyalty offered in full sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him to court by personal edict and richly rewarded him with gold and silk. That was the reward of genuine loyalty.

sentences.zh: 將軍若疑天朝有異論，之鈿請以百口保。

translations.literal: If the General doubts that the Celestial Court has other designs, Zhitian asks to guarantee it with the lives of his hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: If you doubt the dynasty's good faith, I pledge the lives of my entire household as surety.

sentences.zh: 何嫌何疑，而復懷他誌。

translations.literal: What grievance or doubt is there, that you should again harbor other designs?
translations.idiomatic: What cause for grievance or suspicion could there be that you should again turn to rebellion?

sentences.zh: 」獻忠素銜之鈿，遂惡言極罵之。

translations.literal: " Xianzhong had long borne a grudge against Zhitian, and so reviled him with the foulest abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong had long resented Zhitian and now showered him with the vilest curses.

sentences.zh: 之鈿憂憤成病，題數語於壁，自誓以死，遂不視事。

translations.literal: Zhitian, stricken with grief and rage into illness, inscribed several lines on the wall pledging to die, and then ceased attending to his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitian fell ill with grief and indignation, wrote a brief pledge on the wall vowing to die for his duty, and ceased attending to official business.

sentences.zh: 至五月，獻忠果反，劫庫縱囚，毀其城。

translations.literal: By the fifth month Xianzhong did rebel, looted the treasury, released prisoners, and destroyed the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xianzhong rebelled as expected, plundered the treasury, freed the prisoners, and tore down the city walls.

sentences.zh: 之鈿仰藥未絕，獻忠遣使索印，堅不予，賊遂殺之。

translations.literal: Zhitian took poison but had not yet died; Xianzhong sent an emissary to demand his seal; he steadfastly refused to give it, and the bandits then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitian had taken poison but was not yet dead when Xianzhong sent men to demand his official seal. He refused to surrender it, and the rebels killed him.

sentences.zh: 旋縱火焚公署，骸骨為燼。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they set fire to the government office, and his bones were reduced to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: They then set fire to the yamen, and his remains were burned to ash.

sentences.zh: 而大經為賊劫去，不能死。

translations.literal: Dajing, however, was seized by the bandits and could not die.
translations.idiomatic: Dajing was taken captive by the rebels and thus failed to die for his post.

sentences.zh: 迨瑪瑙山戰敗，偕賊將曹威等出降，士論醜之。

translations.literal: When he was defeated at Man'ao Mountain, he came out and surrendered together with the bandit generals Cao Wei and others; public opinion held him in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Man'ao Mountain he surrendered together with the rebel generals Cao Wei and others, and educated opinion despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 之鈿後贈尚寶少卿。

translations.literal: Zhitian was later posthumously enfeoffed as Assistant Director of the Directorate of Imperial Treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitian was later posthumously granted the rank of Assistant Director of the Directorate of Imperial Treasures.

sentences.zh: 郝景春，字和滿，江都人。

translations.literal: Hao Jingchun, courtesy name Heman, was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Jingchun, courtesy name Heman, was a native of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，署鹽城教諭，坐事罷歸。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination, served as acting instructor at Yancheng, and was dismissed and sent home on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination, served as acting instructor at Yancheng, and was dismissed and sent home after an official misconduct case.

sentences.zh: 起陜西苑馬寺萬安監錄事，量移黃州照磨，攝黃安縣事。

translations.literal: He was raised to record keeper at the Wan'an Stud of the Shaanxi Pasturage Commission, later transferred laterally to inspector at Huangzhou, and acted in the affairs of Huang'an County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed record keeper at the Wan'an Stud under the Shaanxi Pasturage Commission, later transferred to inspector at Huangzhou, and placed in charge of Huang'an County affairs.

sentences.zh: 甫三日，群賊奄至，堅守八日夜，始解去。

translations.literal: Only three days after taking office, bandit hordes suddenly arrived; he held firm for eight days and nights before they finally withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Only three days into his tenure bandit hordes suddenly appeared. He held the city for eight days and nights before the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年，擢知房縣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen he was promoted to magistrate of Fang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Chongzhen reign he was promoted to magistrate of Fang County.

sentences.zh: 羅汝才率九營之眾請降於熊文燦，文燦受之。

translations.literal: Luo Rucai led the forces of nine camps to request surrender from Xiong Wen'can, and Wen'can accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Rucai led the men of nine rebel camps to offer surrender to Xiong Wen'can, and Wen'can accepted the terms.

sentences.zh: 汝才猶豫，景春單騎入其營，偕汝才及其黨白貴、黑雲祥歃血盟。

translations.literal: Rucai hesitated; Jingchun rode alone into his camp and, together with Rucai and his followers Bai Gui and Hei Yunxiang, swore a blood oath.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai hesitated, so Jingchun rode alone into his camp and swore a blood oath with Rucai and his lieutenants Bai Gui and Hei Yunxiang.

sentences.zh: 汝才詣軍門降，分諸營於竹谿、保康、上津，而自與貴、雲祥居房縣之野。

translations.literal: Rucai went to the army gate to surrender; the various camps were distributed to Zhuxi, Baokang, and Shangjin, while he himself with Gui and Yunxiang dwelt in the countryside of Fang County.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai then went to the army headquarters to surrender. The various camps were posted to Zhuxi, Baokang, and Shangjin, while he himself remained in the countryside of Fang County with Gui and Yunxiang.

sentences.zh: 當是時，鄖陽諸屬邑，城郭為墟，獨房賴景春拊循，粗可守。

translations.literal: At that time among the subordinate districts of Yunyang the walled towns were mostly ruins; Fang County alone, relying on Jingchun's care and consolation, remained roughly defensible.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the subordinate districts of Yunyang lay in ruins, but Fang County, thanks to Jingchun's care and governance, remained more or less defensible.

sentences.zh: 及大眾雜處，居民日惴惴。

translations.literal: Once the large force was quartered among them, the residents grew daily more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebel masses were encamped among them, the townspeople grew more fearful by the day.

sentences.zh: 景春乃與主簿朱邦聞、守備楊道選修守具，輯諸營。

translations.literal: Jingchun then, together with registrar Zhu Bangwen and garrison commander Yang Daoxuan, prepared defensive equipment and organized the various camps.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchun then worked with registrar Zhu Bangwen and garrison commander Yang Daoxuan to prepare defenses and keep order among the various camps.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，張獻忠反谷城，約汝才同反。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year Zhang Xianzhong rebelled at Gucheng and invited Rucai to rebel together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the following year Zhang Xianzhong rebelled at Gucheng and urged Rucai to join him.

sentences.zh: 景春子鳴鑾，諸生也，力敵萬夫，謂父曰：「吾城當賊沖，而羸卒止二百，城何以守？

translations.literal: Jingchun's son Mingluan, a student, possessed strength to match ten thousand men; he said to his father, "Our city lies in the bandits' path of attack, yet our weakened garrison numbers only two hundred — how can the city be held?
translations.idiomatic: Jingchun's son Mingluan, a licentiate with the strength of ten thousand men, said to his father, "Our city lies directly in the rebels' path, yet we have only two hundred weakened troops. How can we hold it?

sentences.zh: 」乃擐甲詣汝才曰：「若不念香火盟乎？

translations.literal: " He then donned armor and went to Rucai, saying, "Will you not remember the oath sworn before the incense?
translations.idiomatic: He then donned armor and went to Rucai. "Will you not honor the oath we swore before the incense?

sentences.zh: 慎毋從亂。

translations.literal: Take care not to follow rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Take care not to join the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」汝才佯諾。

translations.literal: " Rucai pretended to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 鳴鑾覺其偽，歸與道選授兵登陴，而獻忠所遣前鋒已至，擊斬其將上天龍。

translations.literal: Mingluan perceived the pretense; he returned and, with Daoxuan, armed the troops and mounted the walls. By then the vanguard Xianzhong had dispatched had already arrived, and they struck down and killed its commander Shang Tianlong.
translations.idiomatic: Mingluan saw through the pretense, returned, and with Daoxuan armed the men and manned the walls. Xianzhong's advance guard had already arrived, and they killed its commander Shang Tianlong in battle.

sentences.zh: 遣使縋城乞援於文燦，凡十四往，不報。

translations.literal: They sent messengers down the city wall by rope to beg Wen'can for relief — fourteen times in all — but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: They sent messengers down the city wall by rope to beg Wen'can for reinforcements fourteen times, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 已而賊大至，獻忠兵張白幟，汝才兵張赤幟，俄二幟相雜，環城力攻。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits came in force: Xianzhong's troops raised white banners, Rucai's troops red banners; soon the two colors mingled as they encircled the city and attacked with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels arrived in force. Xianzhong's troops flew white banners and Rucai's red ones; soon the two colors mingled as they encircled the city and attacked with all their might.

sentences.zh: 貴、雲祥策馬呼曰：「以城讓我，保無他也。

translations.literal: Gui and Yunxiang rode up calling out, "Yield the city to us, and we guarantee you no further harm.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Yunxiang rode up shouting, "Hand over the city to us, and we guarantee you will come to no further harm.

sentences.zh: 」獻忠又以張大經檄諭降，景春大罵碎之。

translations.literal: " Xianzhong also used a proclamation from Zhang Dajing to urge surrender; Jingchun cursed loudly and tore it to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong also sent a surrender summons under Zhang Dajing's name. Jingchun cursed it loudly and tore it to shreds.

sentences.zh: 鳴鸞且守且戰，閱五日，賊多死。

translations.literal: Mingluan both defended and fought; after five days many bandits had died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingluan fought on while holding the walls. After five days many rebels had been killed.

sentences.zh: 乃負板穴城，城將崩，鳴鑾熱油灌之。

translations.literal: They brought up mantlets and dug under the wall; as the wall was about to collapse, Mingluan poured boiling oil down upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels brought up mantlets and dug under the wall. As the wall was about to give way, Mingluan poured boiling oil down upon them.

sentences.zh: 又擊傷獻忠左足，殺其所愛善馬。

translations.literal: He also wounded Xianzhong's left foot and killed his favorite good steed.
translations.idiomatic: He also wounded Xianzhong's left foot and killed his favorite warhorse.

sentences.zh: 乃用間入賊壘，陰識獻忠所臥帳，將襲擒之。

translations.literal: He then sent agents to infiltrate the bandit camp, secretly identified the tent where Xianzhong slept, and was about to launch a surprise capture.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent agents into the rebel camp, secretly identified the tent where Xianzhong slept, and prepared a surprise capture.

sentences.zh: 指揮張三錫啟北門揖汝才入，道選巷戰死。

translations.literal: Commander Zhang Sanxi opened the north gate and gestured Rucai inside; Daoxuan died fighting in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhang Sanxi opened the north gate and ushered Rucai in. Daoxuan died fighting in the streets.

sentences.zh: 大經使汝才說景春降，怒不答。

translations.literal: Dajing had Rucai urge Jingchun to surrender; he angrily refused to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Dajing sent Rucai to persuade Jingchun to surrender, but Jingchun angrily refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 問庫藏儲蓄安在，叱曰：「庫藏若有物，城豈為汝陷！

translations.literal: They asked where the treasury stores were kept; he shouted, "If the treasury held anything, how could the city have fallen to you!
translations.idiomatic: They asked where the treasury stores were hidden. He shouted back, "If the treasury held anything worth taking, how could the city have fallen to you!

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，殺一典史、一守備恐之，卒不屈，與鳴鑾俱被殺。

translations.literal: " The bandits in anger killed a clerical aide and a garrison officer to terrify him, yet in the end he would not yield; he and Mingluan were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in fury killed a clerical aide and a garrison officer to intimidate him, but he still refused to submit. He and Mingluan were both killed.

sentences.zh: 仆陳宜赤死之。

translations.literal: His servant Chen Yichi died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His servant Chen Yichi died with him.

sentences.zh: 邦聞及其家人並不屈死。

translations.literal: Bangwen and his entire family likewise refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bangwen and his entire family likewise refused to submit and were killed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈景春尚寶少卿，建祠奉祀，道選等亦贈恤。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Jingchun was posthumously given the title Assistant Director of the Directorate of Imperial Treasures, a shrine was built for his worship, and Daoxuan and the others also received posthumous enfeoffments and condolence awards.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached the court, Jingchun was posthumously granted the rank of Assistant Director of the Directorate of Imperial Treasures, a shrine was erected in his honor, and Daoxuan and the others received posthumous honors and compensation.

sentences.zh: 已，帝召見輔臣賀逢聖，備述其死事狀，改贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor summoned Grand Secretary He Fengsheng, who fully recounted the circumstances of his death; the posthumous rank was changed to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Emperor summoned Grand Secretary He Fengsheng, who gave a full account of Jingchun's death in office. The posthumous rank was raised to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 三錫後為官軍所獲，磔死。

translations.literal: Sanxi was later captured by government troops and executed by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Sanxi was later captured by government troops and executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 張克儉，字禹型，屯留人。

translations.literal: Zhang Kejian, courtesy name Yuxing, was a native of Tunliu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kejian, courtesy name Yuxing, was a native of Tunliu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 授輝縣知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Huixian.

sentences.zh: 六年春，賊犯武安，守備曹鳴鶚戰死，遂犯輝縣。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixth year bandits invaded Wu'an; garrison commander Cao Ming'e died in battle, and they then invaded Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year rebels attacked Wu'an. Garrison commander Cao Ming'e was killed in battle, and the rebels then pressed on to Huixian.

sentences.zh: 克儉乘城固守，賊不能下，屯百泉書院，三日而去。

translations.literal: Kejian mounted the walls and held firm; the bandits could not take the city, encamped at Baiquan Academy for three days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian mounted the walls and held firm. The rebels could not take the city, encamped at Baiquan Academy for three days, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部主事，被薦召對，稱旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to a secretaryship in the Ministry of War; recommended for imperial audience, his responses pleased the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to a secretaryship in the Ministry of War, recommended for an imperial audience, and his answers pleased the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 十二年擢湖廣僉事，監鄖、襄諸軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Huguang and supervised the armies of Yunyang and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Huguang and placed in charge of the armies of Yunyang and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌鎮襄陽，深倚仗之。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang was stationed at Xiangyang and relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang was stationed at Xiangyang and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠、羅汝才之敗也，小秦王、渾世王、過天星等皆降，嗣昌處之房、竹山中，命克儉安輯。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xianzhong and Luo Rucai were defeated, the Little Qin King, Hunshi King, Guotianxing, and others all surrendered; Sichang quartered them in the mountains of Fang and Zhushan and ordered Kejian to settle and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Xianzhong and Luo Rucai were defeated, the Little Qin King, Hunshi King, Guotianxing, and others all surrendered. Sichang quartered them in the mountains of Fang and Zhushan and ordered Kejian to settle and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 而諸賊得免死牌，莫肯散，自擇便地，連營數百里。

translations.literal: But the various bandits, having received death-exemption passes, refused to disperse; they chose convenient locations for themselves and encamped in linked lines for hundreds of li.
translations.idiomatic: But the rebels, having received death-exemption passes, refused to disband. They chose convenient sites for themselves and encamped in linked lines stretching for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 時河南、北大饑，流民就食襄、漢者日數萬，降卒多闌入流民中。

translations.literal: At the time Henan and the north suffered great famine; refugees seeking food in the Xiang and Han regions numbered tens of thousands each day, and many surrendered soldiers slipped in among the refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and the north were then in the grip of famine. Tens of thousands of refugees streamed daily into the Xiang and Han regions seeking food, and many surrendered soldiers mingled among them.

sentences.zh: 克儉深憂之，上書嗣昌曰：「襄陽自古要區，本朝筦鑰獻陵，視昔尤重。

translations.literal: Kejian was deeply troubled and wrote to Sichang, saying, "Xiangyang has from antiquity been a strategic region; in our dynasty it holds the keys to the Xian Mausoleum, and its importance exceeds that of former times.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian was deeply alarmed and wrote to Sichang: "Xiangyang has always been a strategic region. In our dynasty it guards the keys to the Xian Mausoleum, and its importance is greater than ever.

sentences.zh: 近兩河饑民雲集，新舊降丁逼處其間，一夫叫呼，即足致亂。

translations.literal: Recently famine refugees from the two river regions have gathered in clouds; old and new surrendered troops are pressed in among them — one man's shout would suffice to trigger rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Famine refugees from the two river regions have lately gathered in great numbers, and old and new surrendered troops are packed in among them. One man's shout would be enough to set off a revolt.

sentences.zh: 況秦兵以長、武之變，西歸鄖、房。

translations.literal: Moreover the Qin troops, after the Changwu mutiny, have returned west to Yunyang and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after the Changwu mutiny the Shaanxi troops have withdrawn west to Yunyang and Fang.

sentences.zh: 軍府粗立，降營棋置，奚啻放虎自衛。

translations.literal: The military headquarters is barely established, surrendered camps are strewn about like chess pieces — this is no better than using tigers as one's own guard.
translations.idiomatic: The military headquarters is barely in order, surrendered camps are scattered about like chess pieces on a board — this is little better than keeping tigers to guard oneself.

sentences.zh: 紫、漢、西、興，初無重門之備，何恃不恐。

translations.literal: Zi, Han, Xi, and Xing initially have no layered defenses — upon what do they rely that they are not afraid?
translations.idiomatic: Zi, Han, Xi, and Xing have no layered defenses in place. Upon what do they rely that they feel no fear?

sentences.zh: 」嗣昌不以為意，報曰：「昔高仁厚六日降賊百萬，迄擒阡能，監軍何怯耶？

translations.literal: " Sichang did not take it seriously and replied, "In the past Gao Renhou in six days received the surrender of a million bandits and finally captured Qian Neng — why is the military superintendent so timid?
translations.idiomatic: Sichang paid no heed and replied, "In the past Gao Renhou received the surrender of a million bandits in six days and finally captured Qian Neng. Why is the army supervisor so timid?

sentences.zh: 」及嗣昌入蜀，委克儉以留務。

translations.literal: " When Sichang entered Sichuan, he entrusted Kejian with remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichang entered Sichuan, he left Kejian in charge of remaining affairs.

sentences.zh: 錄破賊功，加右參議，監軍如故。

translations.literal: Recording merit for defeating bandits, Kejian was promoted to Right Assistant Commissioner while retaining his military supervision.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in defeating the rebels he was promoted to Right Assistant Commissioner while retaining his army supervision.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以本官移守下川南道，鄖陽巡撫袁繼咸奏留之。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred on his present rank to guard the Lower Southern Sichuan Circuit; Yunyang grand coordinator Yuan Jixian memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred on his present rank to the Lower Southern Sichuan Circuit, but Yunyang grand coordinator Yuan Jixian memorialized the throne to keep him in place.

sentences.zh: 十四年二月擢右僉都御史，巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and appointed Grand Coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourteenth year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and appointed Grand Coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 未聞命，獻忠令人假督府軍符誑入襄陽城。

translations.literal: Before the appointment reached him, Xianzhong had men forge the military tally of the governor-general and deceive their way into Xiangyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointment reached him, Xianzhong had men forge the governor-general's military tally and deceive their way into Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 克儉不能辨，夜分，賊從中起，焚襄王府。

translations.literal: Kejian could not tell the forgery; at midnight the bandits rose from within and burned the Prince of Xiang's palace.
